requestTitle: Improving Explainability in Analyzing AI-Generated Media
abstract: This work proposes an explainable AI-generated media detection system designed to serve both experts and the general public. The framework integrates existing black-box and white-box detectors with explanation techniques, using SHAP for black-box models and Grad-CAM for white-box models, to identify semantic regions critical to model predictions. These regions are further analyzed using a curated library of physical and physiological-based methods, such as corneal specular highlight symmetry and pupil shape regularity, to enhance interpretability without compromising detection reliability. For AI experts, the system supports in-depth assessments through advanced analyses in frequency and residual domains. For non-experts, an information distillation module aggregates and visualizes key artifacts with simplified textual explanations, enabling transparent, accessible evaluation of media authenticity.

requestTitle: Start-Up: Maytal Dahan, Texas Advanced Computing Center
Start-Up: Maytal Dahan, Texas Advanced Computing Center

Out-of-Domain Evaluation of Reasoning Models
abstract: We aim to push Large Language Models (LLMs) beyond their usual training tasks—like solving math problems or writing code—by testing them on challenging “out-of-domain” puzzles. First, we evaluate cutting-edge models (OpenAI o3-pro and o4-mini) on verbal reasoning benchmarks based on the of the NPR Sunday Puzzle. These tests show how well a model can handle intricate, everyday-language problems rather than just math or programming. Next, we extend our focus to concurrency reasoning, where the models must spot and fix mistakes in parallel code. By studying both verbal and concurrency-related tasks, we gain a deeper understanding of each model’s general-purpose problem-solving skills. The final goal is to guide improvements in LLM design so that future models can tackle real-world challenges that require strong reasoning across many domains.

requestTitle: National Deep Inference Fabric
abstract: We seek a year-long, fixed-node allocation on NCSA Delta to run the National Deep Inference Fabric (NDIF), a research-oriented inference service that blends the cost-sharing efficiency of commercial APIs with the full transparency of open-weight models. During Year 1 we sustained NDIF through a series of just-in-time 90-day GPU grants while building NNsight’s internal-inspection tooling and supporting 30+ pilot researchers; that stop-gap approach proved the concept but required constant re-application cycles that cannot support NDIF’s expanded Year 2 charter. A continuous Delta block will replace those brittle renewals with reliable, round-the-clock capacity, letting a projected 200 researchers rerun experiments on demand, reproduce results, and explore a catalog that will grow from 8 to 100+ models (including forthcoming DeepSeek 607 B) via our hot-swap scheduler. The allocation thus safeguards scientific continuity, scales a uniquely transparent AI platform to national reach, and keeps NDIF’s per-user costs on par with commercial services while delivering capabilities those services cannot—layer-level inspection, activation editing, and gradient capture on models as large as 405 B parameters.

requestTitle: Towards Agentic LLM for Chiplet Design
abstract: The goal of this project is to build an agentic AI model for end-to-end electronic design automation (EDA), spanning HDL generation, verification, and physical layout. Our framework builds upon Reinforcement Learning from Internal Feedback (RLIF), which learns chip design tasks without the need of external labels. Prior work shows that RLIF achieves ~15% gains in code tasks, and our own preliminary experiments (based on Qwen3-14B) demonstrate an 8% lift on Verilog-Eval2. Our approach is promising for chip design, a domain with scarce open-source data. By fine-tuning base models with RLIF and integrating verification agents (waveform-guided checks) and back-end tasks (synthesis, placement&routing), we aim to develop and automate workflows across the design stack with a unified, open-source EDA toolchain. Our framework will further enable power-performance optimizations from natural language interfaces.

requestTitle: Trustworthy and Secure Cloud-Native Agentic OpenROAD
abstract: We propose OpenROAD V2, a cloud-native, AI-assisted extension of the DARPA-funded OpenROAD IC EDA tool. Our goal is to improve the efficacy, trust, and security of agentic systems for chip design. Three main foci include parallelizability, structured telemetry, and GPU acceleration. OpenROAD V2 will expose design and code “knobs” in a controlled, declarative way, allowing LLM-guided agents to tune tool behavior without unsafe arbitrary edits. These innovations will enable runtime improvements of 3-10X and PPA gains of 15-20%, while providing a trusted “sandbox” for AI agents to self-adapt OpenROAD flows to specific technologies and designs. This work will establish a foundation for ML-driven and agentic EDA research, opening new opportunities in chip design research, education and industrial practice.

requestTitle: Braingents: Developing a Longitudinal Agentic AI Framework for Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Biomarkers
abstract:
Alzheimer’s disease remains a major unmet challenge, with neuroimaging biomarkers offering critical insight into early detection and progression. However, current analysis pipelines require extensive manual intervention across fragmented tools, creating barriers to both research scalability and clinical translation.

We propose Braingents, an agentic AI framework that autonomously orchestrates end-to-end neuroimaging analysis while preserving expert-level accuracy. Braingents brings together four specialized agents: a Data Harmonization Agent that normalizes scanner and protocol variability across sites using domain adaptation; a Multi-Modal Detection Agent leveraging vision transformers to quantify structural atrophy and amyloid/tau burden; a Longitudinal Tracking Agent for precise monitoring of hippocampal volumes, cortical thinning, and plaque progression; and a Clinical Reasoning Agent that generates interpretable, language model–driven reports.

By combining automation, interpretability, and multimodal scalability, Braingents addresses current bottlenecks and aims to accelerate biomarker discovery while paving the way for clinical readiness in Alzheimer’s disease neuroimaging.

requestTitle: RxFM: A Multimodal Foundation Model for ALS Therapeutic Science and Drug Discovery
abstract: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neurodegenerative disease with no cure and a complex, multifactorial etiology. Traditional single-target approaches have failed to yield effective ALS therapies, except for rare single-gene targets, e.g. SOD1. New AI-driven strategies can now address ALS’s heterogeneous pathophysiology as a network perturbation problem. We propose a Multimodal Therapeutic Foundation Model (RxFM), trained on diverse biomedical and pharmacodynamic data and harnessed to accelerate ALS drug discovery and drug repurposing. This RxFM model will integrate multi-omic, single-cell, metabolomic, clinical, and drug perturbation data within a unified framework. Such a holistic model that incorporates drug perturbation effects can identify therapeutic interventions that reverse disease signatures. Our approach is novel and ambitious, extending advances in biologic foundation models to model therapeutic actions. Moreover, the RxFM framework can be fine-tuned or queried for diseases with little known biology, supporting zero-shot drug discovery. Timeline: We expect to complete this Rx-FM in 9 months and submit 2 publications within 12 months.

requestTitle: Accelerating molecular design and crystal structure prediction for carbon capture
abstract: Crystal structure prediction (CSP) is a longstanding challenge in materials science, with conventional methods relying on computationally expensive density functional theory (DFT) calculations that limit their applicability to small systems. Recent advances in machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) and generative AI offer a paradigm shift, enabling efficient exploration of vast configuration spaces with near-DFT accuracy at greatly reduced cost. We propose to develop an integrated AI-driven CSP workflow that combines MLIPs, generative AI, DFT, and classical simulations to predict the crystal structures of complex organic systems, demonstrating our workflow on polyamine molecular crystals as promising candidates for carbon capture. The resulting workflow and transferable MLIPs will be made publicly available, providing powerful new tools for CSP of molecular crystals and accelerating the discovery of materials for energy and environmental applications.

requestTitle: Accelerating Multifunctional C-S-H Seeding Materials Discovery through Agentic AI and Scalable Cloud Computing
abstract: Concrete is the most widely used man-made material globally, with its composition and production methods largely unchanged for over 200 years. Cement production is responsible for nearly 8% of total CO2 emissions. In developed nations, infrastructure repair is a major challenge, and the U.S. alone requires $2.8 trillion for its aging transportation systems. Low-carbon cements could reduce emissions by 20-60%, but they struggle with early-age strength development, hindering their adoption. Research on calcium-silicate-hydrate (C-S-H) seeding has shown promise in accelerating cement hydration, highlighting the need for new multifunctional C-S-H seeding materials. This proposal aims to develop an innovative artificial intelligence (AI) pipeline that integrates advanced AI techniques with domain-specific constraints and physics-based simulations to discover and optimize novel C-S-H seeding materials.

requestTitle: Start-Up: Qing Ye, Sostos LLC
PEFT-CE: Parameter-Efficient Early-Exit Fine-Tuning for Cloud-Edge Collaborative Large Language Models
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable performance in Natural Language Processing (NLP). However, the prevalent cloud-based LLM deployment for providing LLM-based services at the edge faces several critical challenges, including high operational costs, inherent network latency, and service interruptions due to network disconnection. While cloud-edge collaborative LLM deployments have emerged to address these issues by distributing computation between the edge and the cloud, existing methods suffer from significant accuracy drops when operating in edge standalone mode, disconnected from the cloud. This project proposes a novel Parameter-Efficient Early-Exit Fine-Tuning framework for Cloud-Edge collaborative LLMs (PEFT-CE). PEFT-CE is designed to substantially enhance the accuracy of LLMs in cloud-edge collaborative deployments, particularly in edge standalone mode. We will systematically investigate effective knowledge distillation strategies, fused loss functions, and parameter-efficient fine-tuning techniques (e.g., LoRA) to optimize LLM accuracy across both edge standalone and cloud-edge collaborative modes. The resulting open-source PEFT-CE framework will enable edge devices to deliver high-quality and independent LLM inference even under unstable network conditions, with optional cloud support. This design will significantly reduce operational costs for LLM service providers and accelerate the widespread adoption of LLM-based services in real-world resource-constrained environments. This project will address two NAIRR Pilot cross-cutting focus areas by (1) creating or developing open-source AI tools, models, and methods for efficient, accurate, and resilient LLM deployment and (2) by training and educating the next generation AI-savvy workforce.

requestTitle: PRISM: Public Reproducible Infrastructure for Safety and Measurement of Generative AI
abstract:
Trustworthy generative AI requires evaluation that is reproducible, threat-model aware, and fast enough to keep pace with frontier systems. We propose PRISM, a public evaluation and safety infrastructure focused on three pillars: alignment and truthfulness, provenance and watermark robustness, and agentic reasoning. PRISM unifies widely used and emerging benchmarks in an open harness, adds missing stress tests that reflect real deployment risks, and operates a living leaderboard with transparent uncertainty and audit trails.
Our team’s prior assets include HallusionBench for visual-illusion-induced hallucination, WAVES for watermark robustness, Mementos for reasoning over image sequences, and Easy2Hard-Bench for standardized difficulty profiling, plus auditing of false refusals (PHTest). We will extend these into v2 suites, integrate leading agent tasks (web and tool use), and publish standard APIs so researchers and industry can evaluate models and defenses side by side.
We request GPU-hours distributed across NCSA DeltaAI (GH200/H100), SDSC Expanse AI (H100), NCSA Delta GPU (A100/A40), and Purdue Anvil (A100/H100) as well as state of the art model API accesses. This mix provides interactive headroom for agents and long-context workloads while enabling cross-architecture checks important for national benchmarking. Outputs include: (1) open datasets and stress tests; (2) a containerized evaluation harness and APIs; (3) a public leaderboard that surfaces capability-safety trade-offs; and (4) short community reports aligned with standards and policy discussions.
PRISM fits the NAIRR Pilot’s mission to broaden access to compute and shared data for safe, reliable AI research while keeping the ask clearly at pilot scale.

requestTitle: Streaming Long-Video Understanding with Grounding and Efficient Memory
abstract: This project aims to advance the foundations of streaming video understanding by developing models capable of perceiving every frame in long, untrimmed video streams—a critical requirement for real-world agents such as autonomous systems, assistive devices, and surveillance platforms. Unlike existing vision-language models that rely on sparse sampling or short clips, our approach focuses on continuous, frame-level reasoning with efficient memory and grounded predictions to avoid hallucinations. By integrating open-vocabulary grounding and compressed memory modules, this work will enable real-time, semantically rich perception across extended timescales, laying the groundwork for intelligent systems that are robust, adaptive, and contextually aware.

requestTitle: Start-Up: Cheng Zhang, Texas A&M University
NAIRR Pilot Classroom Request: GPU Resources for CSC 426 Deep Learning
abstract: This project integrates NAIRR Pilot computing resources into CSC 426: Deep Learning, an upper-level computer science course at Northern Kentucky University. The course provides students with hands-on experience in training and deploying modern neural networks, such as convolutional, recurrent, and transformer-based architectures. Access to GPU-accelerated computing and shared storage will allow students to work with real-world datasets and state-of-the-art frameworks such as PyTorch and TensorFlow, bridging theory with practice in ways not possible on limited local infrastructure. By leveraging NAIRR resources, the course will expand equitable access to advanced AI tools, giving all students the opportunity to complete assignments and capstone projects.

requestTitle: Start-Up: Esther Rodriguez Hernandez, Arizona State University
A Vision–Language Framework for Clinically Grounded Medical Image Segmentation Explanations
abstract: Medical image segmentation is a critical step in diagnosing and monitoring conditions such as brain tumors, stroke, and multiple sclerosis. While deep learning models have achieved expert-level performance in segmenting these images, their “black box” nature remains a major barrier to clinical adoption. Current explainability methods, such as heatmaps or saliency maps, fall short because they lack clarity and clinical context. In this project, we propose a new approach that makes segmentation models both accurate and interpretable by embedding symbolic reasoning and natural language explanations into the segmentation process. Our method converts image features into structured symbolic tokens and uses a vision–language framework to generate clinically meaningful explanations, such as describing why a specific region was segmented based on MRI characteristics. By aligning AI decisions with clinical reasoning, this work aims to improve transparency, trust, and usability of medical imaging AI in real-world healthcare settings.

requestTitle: Discovering Scaling Laws for Large-Scale Machine Learning in Molecular Simulations
abstract:
Our proposed research will develop scalable machine learning (ML) methods that advance computational chemistry and molecular simulation, overcoming the limitations of current graph neural network (GNN)-based methods. Specifically, we aim to establish clear empirical scaling laws for Transformer-based models that do not rely on graph representations, enabling the efficient and predictable training of large-scale ML models for atomistic simulations. Achieving this goal requires novel methodological development to determine optimal molecular tokenization schemes and positional encoding strategies, ensuring that Transformer architectures effectively capture chemical and spatial information in molecular data.
Such models will significantly enhance our ability to accurately simulate complex molecular systems, accelerating discoveries in drug design, biomolecular engineering, and materials science. Our project is timely, as the recent release of the Open Molecules 2025 dataset (developed by Meta AI, our team, and other university and national lab partners) presents immediate opportunities to test our methods.

requestTitle: Securing LLMs against Prompt Injection Attacks
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are widely deployed as the backend for numerous real-world applications. However, due to the lack of a clear separation between instructions and data within prompts, LLMs are highly vulnerable to prompt injection attacks. Specifically, when data originates from untrusted external sources such as the Internet, an attacker can embed malicious prompts. As a result, the LLM may follow the injected instructions and produce attacker-controlled responses. Prompt injection attacks pose severe security and safety risks to LLMs; for example, OWASP ranks prompt injection as the number one threat in its Top 10 security risks for LLMs. Our ultimate goal is to make LLMs secure against prompt injection attacks. To achieve this, we will pursue a holistic approach that comprises three interconnected research tasks: we will systematically investigate the security vulnerabilities of LLMs to prompt injection attacks, develop defenses to prevent such attacks, and create methods to detect and localize prompt injection attempts.

Prompt injection attacks pose severe security and safety risks to LLMs; for example, OWASP ranks prompt injection as the number one threat in its Top 10 security risks for LLMs. Our ultimate goal is to make LLMs secure against prompt injection attacks. To achieve this, we will pursue a holistic approach that comprises three interconnected research tasks: we will systematically investigate the security vulnerabilities of LLMs to prompt injection attacks, develop defenses to prevent such attacks, and create methods to detect and localize prompt injection attempts.

requestTitle: Reasoning and Adaptation for Trustworthy Scientific and Safety-Critical AI
abstract:
This proposal advances trustworthy AI for specialized domains through two synergistic thrusts: (1) Safety in Evolving Contexts, which enables AI models to flexibly incorporate new safety policies, guidelines, and instruction hierarchies at inference time without requiring costly retraining; and
(2) Grounded Scientific Agents, which empower AI systems to assist researchers and clinicians by reasoning over scientific and medical evidence in a transparent, verifiable way. In Thrust 1, we introduce foundational techniques for adapting large language models (LLMs) to dynamic environments using hypernetworks and instruction-prioritization reasoning.
In Thrust 2, we apply these adaptable models to science and medicine, building agents that help evaluate hypotheses, search biomedical knowledge, and support evidence-grounded reasoning. Together, these thrusts aim to enable context-aware, trustworthy AI that can respond to evolving safety needs and provide rigorous support in scientific domains, without requiring retraining.

requestTitle: Example-Free Test-Time Adaptation from Task Guidelines
abstract: This work explores a new way to make large language models (LLMs) more flexible and easier to use. Instead of training them with many examples for each new task, we aim to let LLMs adapt by simply reading and following task guidelines written in natural language. This is similar to how people can follow written guidelines without needing lots of practice. While current methods like LoRA (Low Rank Adaptation) allow efficient tuning, they still require labeled data and careful finetuning. Our approach reduces this complexity by helping models understand tasks on the fly, improving usability and lowering the cost of applying LLMs to new tasks.

requestTitle: VizFold: Visualizing & Interpretable Protein Folding in AlphaFold and Similar Protein Models
abstract:
Artificial intelligence (AI) advancements are transforming scientific discovery, enabling breakthroughs that were once thought unattainable. AI-driven models like AlphaFold have revolutionized protein structure prediction in biology, achieving unprecedented accuracy in determining 3-dimensional structures from amino acid sequences. This capability has opened the door to applications ranging from drug discovery to protein engineering. Despite these successes, the inner workings of such models remain a black box, hindering their broader scientific utility and the development of fundamental theories. This project aims to illuminate the internal activity and their correspondence to bio-physical principles by developing advanced visualization and interpretability tools. These tools will allow researchers to gain unprecedented insights into how these AI models operate, fostering a deeper understanding of protein folding processes. By providing open-source software and an interactive Science Gateway, the project will democratize access to these capabilities, empowering a wider range of scientists to explore and refine protein folding theories and showcasing the role of AI in advancing fundamental scientific knowledge.

VizFold tackles the critical challenge of understanding and interpreting the mechanisms underpinning protein folding predictions made by AI models like AlphaFold. While these models excel at accurately predicting protein structures, their processes and principles remain opaque, limiting their broader applicability and the development of scientific theories. To bridge this gap, the project focuses on three key objectives. First, it will develop visualization tools to examine activation propagation within the specialized architectural components, including attention mechanisms and structure modules unique to AlphaFold-like models. Second, it will enhance interpretability by applying probing techniques, dimensionality reduction, and Layerwise Relevance Propagation to elucidate how these models encode folding processes. Third, it will build an interactive Science Gateway powered by Cybershuttle, enabling researchers to visualize and analyze model outputs in real-time while offloading computational tasks to high-performance infrastructure. By achieving these goals, VizFold will advance computational biology, support non-expert users, and lay the foundation for a new physical-chemical understanding of protein folding, paving the way for future innovations in AI-driven science.

requestTitle: Complex-Vector Cross-Token-Context Transformers for Efficient Large Language Models
abstract: We propose a physics-inspired, highly efficient large language model (LLM) architecture, the Complex-Vector Cross-Token-Context Transformer (CVC-Transformer), that boosts the performance on downstream tasks such as language inference, abstract generation, and open-ended text generation while reducing its computational resource requirements.

requestTitle: Meta-Learning for Robust Foundation Model Adaptation
abstract: The inference-time compute paradigm of large foundation models has unlocked remarkable performance across diverse tasks. However, these large foundation models still remain vulnerable to adversarial prompt manipulations, particularly due to their sequential input processing. This project proposes a meta-learning framework to enhance foundation model robustness by addressing two critical challenges at inference time: adversarial prompt ordering and semantic manipulation. First, we introduce a meta-reinforcement learning system that adaptively filters prompt sequences, dynamically controlling attention and data inclusion based on learned policies. Second, we develop a defensive prompt rewriting module that restructures inputs to neutralize adversarial patterns while preserving user intent. Together, these mechanisms aim to improve the safety and trustworthiness of large foundation models in interactive applications

requestTitle: Efficient Test-time Alignment for Scientific Foundation Models
abstract:
Scientific foundation models, such as molecular language models and medical multimodal models, are becoming vital tools in domains like drug discovery and clinical decision support. Ensuring that these models generate outputs that align with domain-specific scientific constraints is critical for their safe, reliable, and effective use. Current alignment methods, such as reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), require costly retraining and assume fixed objectives, making them ill-suited for dynamic scientific environments.

This project proposes a new test-time alignment framework that aligns model outputs during inference, without modifying the underlying model. By combining probabilistic modeling with Monte Carlo sampling, the approach offers a plug-and-play mechanism to enforce alignment constraints flexibly and efficiently. This method is applicable across a range of scientific tasks and model architectures, enabling reliable adaptation to evolving requirements in real-world scientific workflows.

requestTitle: General Purpose Technologies and the Evolution of Science: Evidence from the Early Computers
abstract:
Digital computers rank among the most transformative general-purpose technologies of the twentieth century, yet we still know remarkably little about how it transformed science and how scientists actually used computers in day-to-day research during their formative decades. We assemble the first comprehensive database of university computer installations in the United States up to 1971 and merge it with the full publication record of affiliated scholars. Preliminary results using computer-related keyword screening of OpenAlex papers show diffusion of computers was fast but uneven. Physical sciences dominated initial adoption, with computer users gaining significant citation advantages. Computer access increased publication output and impact across universities, with computer-keyword matched papers displaying a citation premium of around 20%. 

Our project aims to incorporate AI and LLMs to go beyond simple keyword matching and classify millions of research papers from full text to determine how computers transformed scientific work—whether by replacing existing methods or enabling entirely new research—and how adoption patterns varied across disciplines, providing historical context for today's AI integration in science.

Automating the Design of Data Extraction Workflows to Accelerate Scientific Discovery
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) offer transformative potential for accelerating scientific discovery, particularly by extracting experimental data from the vast and growing body of unstructured scientific literature. However, designing effective information extraction (IE) tasks—identifying what data to extract, assessing its presence in text, and determining whether a model can extract it accurately—remains a time-consuming and expertise-heavy process. This project aims to develop an intelligent assistant that helps scientists rapidly design and validate new IE tasks for extracting experimental data from document collections, enabling faster and more reliable synthesis of scientific knowledge. The assistant will combine schema generation and performance prediction models—trained on open-weight LLMs—with API-based frontier models such as GPT-4o to perform large-scale extractions and evaluate system outputs. By enabling researchers to assess task feasibility before investing in annotation or model development, this work will reduce the cost and delay of transforming scientific literature into structured, machine-actionable datasets. Resources are requested to support large-scale LLM inference and model fine-tuning on scientific corpora. All tools and datasets will be released openly to support the broader scientific and AI research communities.

requestTitle: AI Foundation Model for Lunar Science Applications
abstract:
The Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (LROC) archive—spanning over 1.1 petabytes—constitutes the most extensive high-resolution dataset in planetary science. Despite its scientific richness, much of this data remains underutilized due to its immense scale and complexity. This proposal introduces the Lunar Foundation Model (LFM), a general-purpose AI model trained on the full LROC dataset, designed to accelerate key lunar science applications, including automated crater detection, polar resource identification, terrain understanding, and mission planning.
We propose a multi-stage methodology involving the generation of Analysis Ready Data (ARD) in partnership with the USGS, followed by large-scale self-supervised pretraining, fine-tuning for downstream scientific tasks, and public dissemination of models and tools. The LFM will enable scalable, generalizable inference across a wide range of lunar research needs.
Committed to open science, the project will make all datasets, code, and models freely available, supporting reproducibility and inclusive access. The NAIRR Pilot presents an ideal platform for this work—not only by providing the required petabyte-scale storage and multi-million GPU-hour compute capacity, but also by fostering cross-institutional collaboration and community engagement. Through NAIRR, we will publish the large-scale ML-ready lunar datasets, train users to fine-tune the model, and enable broader scientific communities to engage with and build upon this foundation. This initiative is a joint effort with NASA GSFC, SETI Institute, NASA ARC, The University of Alabama Huntsville, NASA MSFC, USGS. It exemplifies the collaborative, transparent, and high-impact goals of the NAIRR vision.

requestTitle: Decoding Cell Behavior with AI-Powered Virtual Cell Models
abstract: We propose Omnicell, an AI foundation model trained on 150+ million cells to predict cellular responses to genetic and chemical perturbations. Using novel architecture combining generative distribution embeddings with graph neural networks, Omnicell will simulate experiments currently impossible at scale. The project will create the Virtual Cell Atlas—an open resource simulating gene manipulation effects across all cell types and diseases. This enables researchers to computationally screen millions of potential drug targets before laboratory testing, accelerating therapeutic discovery. All models, code, and datasets will be publicly released, democratizing access to advanced cellular modeling for precision medicine and drug development.

requestTitle: Mitigating the Hallucination Tax: Trustworthy Reinforcement Finetuning for LLMs
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) achieve impressive reasoning performance by post-training, such as through Reinforcement Finetuning (RFT). This powerful technique can align LLMs with task-specific goals, particularly in domains such as mathematics and code generation where correctness is well defined. But at the same time, LLMs can be overconfident where they confidently answer ambiguous or unsolvable questions instead of admitting uncertainty. In this work, we aim to identify and systematically study a critical side effect of RFT, which we term the hallucination tax: a degradation in refusal behavior causing models to produce hallucinated answers to unanswerable questions confidently.

requestTitle: NAIRR: Physically-Grounded Geospatial AI for Understanding Complex Global Phenomena
abstract: This project aims to transform the capabilities of Geospatial AI (GeoAI) for the physical sciences by integrating geophysical process models in geospatial foundation models  trained on Earth Observation data. Our integrated approach seeks to enhance performance of AI for Earth Observation models in the face of data limitations like sparse temporal and spatial sampling of observed data, and reveal new data-driven links between atmospheric, oceanic, and land processes.

requestTitle: Self-Supervised Segmentation and Physics-Guided Diffusion Synthesis Using Vision Transformers for Quality Control in Laser Additive Manufacturing
abstract: This project aims to advance autonomous quality control in additive manufacturing by leveraging recent breakthroughs in transformer-based computer vision and generative AI. Focusing on laser-based processes such as Directed Energy Deposition (DED) and Powder Bed Fusion (PBF-L), we will adapt and fine-tune foundation-model-aligned architectures—including Masked Autoencoders (MAE), Vision Transformers (ViT), and the Segment Anything Model (SAM)—to perform defect detection and segmentation on thermal and X-ray computed tomography (XCT) imaging data. Additionally, we will develop a physics-informed diffusion model to synthetically generate rare defect patterns, enhancing anomaly detection performance under data-scarce conditions. The trained models will be optimized for real-time deployment and edge compatibility, laying the groundwork for intelligent, self-correcting manufacturing systems. This work contributes to the emerging ecosystem of foundation models in manufacturing and supports scalable, resource-efficient AI development using NAIRR infrastructure.

requestTitle: Speaker Static Trait Disentanglement for Speaker Anonymization
abstract: Speaker identity protection has become a critical concern in today’s society where human voices can be easily recognized, analyzed and cloned by advanced speech processing techniques. This project aims to develop static vocal trait (e.g., sex, age, accent) disentanglement techniques that allow independent control of these traits for voice anonymization applications. This technique will be helpful for safeguarding user privacy without compromising speech intelligibility or semantic content, and for various speech synthesis applications in education, entertainment and healthcare.

requestTitle: NAIRR Classroom Proposal
abstract:
This project seeks to provide graduate students in Computer Science at California State University, East Bay with access to GPU-backed compute and curated datasets through the NAIRR Pilot. Students enrolled in a machine learning and computer vision course will gain the ability to train, fine-tune, and deploy state-of-the-art multimodal vision-language models (VLMs). These resources are essential for students to engage with the current generation of AI systems, as local infrastructure only supports limited experimentation with small-scale models that do not reflect contemporary capabilities.

By leveraging NAIRR resources, students will complete course projects that include both fine-tuning large multimodal models and developing proof-of-concept applications that demonstrate inference capabilities across vision and text domains. This applied experience will equip students with workforce-ready skills in advanced AI, expand faculty capacity to deliver cutting-edge instruction, and provide equitable access to responsible AI experimentation. We also intend to use this initial experience as a foundation for extending the use of NAIRR-supported resources into other machine learning courses, amplifying the long-term educational impact across the program. The project directly supports NAIRR’s mission to broaden participation in AI education and to ensure that future professionals are trained with the tools and infrastructure necessary to address real-world challenges.

requestTitle: Fine-grained biological trait-aware foundation model
abstract:
Imageomics is a new scientific field where computational tools are built around biological knowledge bases and used to analyze biological image data in order to characterize patterns and gain insights into traits and relationships at individual, population, and species scales. We have successfully collaborated with NAIRR in the development of BioCLIP 2, where 214 million images are used to train a foundation model for organismal biology images. BioCLIP 2 not only achieves state-of-the-art species classification performance but also shows emergent properties of aligning ecological relationships and separating intra-species variations. The project is well aligned with the scope of NAIRR—use scaled training for scientific domains. In this application, we aim to further extend the BioCLIP series and design specialist models focusing on fine-grained biological visual trait understanding. The project has two main components:

requestTitle: HWER-UTD Teaching Clinical Training Simulator: Developing an AI-Agent-Based Virtual System for Better Teacher Preparation
abstract: Texas school districts continue to face a critical shortage of qualified teachers in science and math, especially in subjects like physics, chemistry, and mathematics. To address this challenge, HomeWorld Educational Resources (HWER) and UTeach Dallas are developing the Teaching Clinical Training Simulator (TCTS)—an immersive, AI-powered platform designed to prepare future STEM teachers through realistic, hands-on simulations. Unlike traditional teacher training tools that focus only on classroom instruction, TCTS replicates the full teaching experience, including everyday interactions with students, parents, school administrators, and fellow educators. Built using cutting-edge AI technologies—including large language models for generating dynamic conversations, diffusion models for creating visual classroom scenes, and rule-based systems for simulating student performance—TCTS offers a role-playing, game-like environment that mirrors real-world teaching. This safe, private, and cost-effective platform allows student teachers in their final year at UTeach Dallas to build confidence and gain experience before entering the workforce. By combining the strengths of the proven UTeach model with scalable, AI-enhanced training, TCTS has the potential to boost recruitment, accelerate teacher readiness, and support long-term retention—particularly in high-need districts. This innovative approach not only improves how teachers are trained but also strengthens the pipeline of future science and math educators across Texas.

requestTitle: Task-based Tabular Search Made Useful
abstract: Massive data lakes hold the promise of groundbreaking discoveries by integrating diverse datasets—such as linking bird song and noise pollution data to study behavioral changes during COVID, or combining credit and economic data to improve loan predictions. Yet, these discoveries are limited by a core bottleneck: the difficulty of finding and evaluating useful datasets. Current dataset search systems rely on keyword queries or surface-level similarity, forcing users to manually filter, download, and test each candidate—an inefficient process that wastes the potential of these rich data repositories. This project aims to transform dataset search by using the user’s data task—like a machine learning prediction or a causal analysis—as the search query. Our system efficiently identifies datasets that concretely improve analytic outcomes, such as increasing prediction accuracy or uncovering causal relationships, by using specialized indexing and learning mechanisms. By coupling dataset discovery with real analytic value, we reduce the friction of data reuse and create a feedback loop that helps both data users and providers improve data quality over time. We will extend this system to support more complex queries, improve data integration using large language models within a fixed compute budget, and explore the verification of causal claims in scientific research using data lakes. With NAIRR resources, we aim to deploy this system as a public service to make data repositories more actionable and accessible to researchers and practitioners.

requestTitle: Foundational Graph Retrieval for Retrieval-augmented Generation
abstract: Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems (GraphRAGs) have shown promise in enhancing downstream tasks by leveraging external knowledge from graph-structured data. While widely adopted in domains such as social networks, drug discovery, and scientific research, existing approaches often rely on proximity-based retrieval rules that fail to generalize across diverse graph types and task requirements. This paper advocates for a Foundational Graph Retrieval Model that embraces structural and task heterogeneity by adopting a mixture-of-experts framework. Each expert specializes in a distinct retrieval rule, enabling the system to dynamically align query intents with relevant graph patterns. A reinforcement learning-based controller further refines retrieval strategies through iterative feedback and summarization. By unifying modular retrieval capabilities with adaptive learning, our proposed model offers a scalable and versatile foundation for graph-based retrieval, empowering a broad range of applications, including personalized recommendation, property-driven molecule design, and structure-aware scientific discovery.

requestTitle: Multi-Agent Preference Optimization for Dialogical Reasoning in Large Language Models
abstract:
This project explores new methods for training large language models (LLMs) to engage in advanced forms of dialogical reasoning—enabling AI systems to better understand, evaluate, and generate multi-perspective arguments. Building on recent breakthroughs in AI alignment and multi-agent simulation, the proposed research introduces a novel training framework where LLMs interact in structured dialogues and receive turn-by-turn feedback to improve their reasoning process, rather than simply optimizing for final answers.

By leveraging multiple AI agents that debate or deliberate over complex topics, this work aims to develop models that are more truthful, transparent, and capable of collaborative problem-solving. The project will investigate how structured peer interaction and iterative evaluation can lead to safer and more reliable AI systems. The outcomes have broad implications for educational technology, human-AI collaboration, and the development of AI systems that can engage in civil discourse, support critical thinking, and assist in high-stakes decision-making.

abstract:
This project builds an artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure that enhances access to computational power, datasets, and models that support research on social policy and poverty. It will develop a novel trustworthy AI infrastructure that will 1) integrate, curate, and process policy-related data sets; 2) develop and facilitate access to novel AI models that can learn from existing policies, providing insights such as what makes a program successful; and 3) open new areas of research and scholarship, creating multi-disciplinary communities of policymakers, economists, computer scientists, and government and non-government organizations to better address these societal challenges.

This project demonstrates how the resources made available through the National Artificial Intelligence Research Resource (NAIRR) Pilot program can be employed to address a major social challenge - poverty. The effort develops a novel, trustworthy AI infrastructure that combines the power of foundation models (FM) with the reasoning capabilities of probabilistic graphical models (PGM) for evidence-based poverty eradication research. This project mitigates several technical challenges related to data, models, and their evaluation, providing foundational and use-inspired advances by: 1) Developing novel methods to build a knowledge database from unstructured poverty eradication literature, such as academic literature and impact evaluations; and 2) Combining the linguistic capabilities of LLMs with the reasoning capabilities of a PGM to answer policy-relevant questions.

requestTitle: Northeastern University - Engineering LLM-Integrated Systems
abstract:
Generative AI has raised our expectations of what is possible with software. The previous generation of AI assistants had a narrow set of skills and limited fluency in natural language. However, recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have shown that it is possible to build software systems with a far more natural and fluid interface. In this course, we will study the software engineering foundations for LLM-integrated systems. Students will learn how to build these systems, integrate them with existing software, rigorously test their behavior, and understand their failure modes and limitations.

abstract: The Intelligent Data Exploring Assistant (IDEA) project is advancing how geoscientists interact with complex environmental datasets by combining large language models (LLMs) with domain-specific expertise. Building on an initial prototype called the Station Explorer Assistant (SEA), IDEA integrates natural language querying, data analysis tools, and user feedback mechanisms to create a more intuitive and trustworthy research experience. The project will develop new methods to improve LLM accuracy, validate results through supervisory models, and incorporate domain knowledge via retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). By making advanced geoscience data exploration more accessible through API credits for using state-of-the-art LLMs, this project will accelerate research through deploying new IDEAs, support coastal resilience studies, and foster broader participation in AI-driven science. All outcomes, including software and findings, will be openly shared to maximize public benefit.

requestTitle: A Foundation Model for Global Air Quality Monitoring
abstract:
Air pollution exposure, particularly to PM2.5, O3, NO2, and SO2, represents a leading global health threat requiring accurate, timely monitoring for effective public health intervention and policy development. This project addresses three critical research questions: Can we efficiently model global pollution fields to generate high-resolution predictions and forecasts with uncertainty quantification? Can low-cost sensors enhance prediction accuracy? And can embeddings from remote sensing foundation models improve local forecasting capabilities?

We propose an innovative three-stage, end-to-end deep learning framework that represents the first method to derive global pollutant fields directly from remote observations and ground-based measurements while incorporating fine-scale predictors and uncertainty quantification. The modular approach combines learned data assimilation from satellite and sensor observations, regional-scale downscaling using neural processes, and spatiotemporal forecasting with transformers. This encoder-processor-decoder architecture integrates diverse data sources including satellite observations (MODIS, TROPOMI, VIIRS, GOSAT, Himawari, Sentinel-5P), meteorological reanalysis, reference-grade and low-cost ground sensors, and embeddings from remote sensing foundation models to generate high-resolution, uncertainty-aware predictions and forecasts.

The scientific merit lies in providing a unified, physics-aware framework that efficiently generates fast, high-resolution, uncertainty-aware predictions without computationally expensive numerical solvers—requiring three orders of magnitude less compute than traditional models like CAMS. This represents the first integration of low-cost sensors in global pollution monitoring and the first end-to-end approach combining satellite data assimilation, neural process downscaling.

Resource Requirements: 120,000 H100 GPU-hours on NCSA DeltaAI and 30TB disk storage for multi-decade global datasets.

requestTitle: Streaming Voice Transformation for Voice Privacy Protection
abstract: The rapid development of speech synthesis techniques (e.g., voice cloning) has raised significant concerns on voice privacy. A scientific/technical approach to addressing this problem is to develop voice anonymization techniques that can transform a speaker’s voice without altering the linguistic content or affecting the naturalness of speech. Existing research on voice transformation has achieved good performance in offline settings but fails in streaming settings. This project aims to advance streaming voice transformation research to meet real-time application needs while achieving comparable quality and naturalness as offline methods.

requestTitle: A Multi-Modal Foundation Model for Agentic Chemical Discovery
abstract: While foundation models offer immense potential for accelerating chemical discovery, current models often treat modalities in isolation or lack sophisticated agentic reasoning capabilities. This project introduces ChemForge, a pioneering foundation model designed to bridge this gap. ChemForge will unify state-of-the-art open-source LLMs and molecular foundation models, through continued pre-training, multi-modal alignment, and reasoning-oriented fine-tuning. It features two defining capabilities: 1) Unified Multi-Modal Chemical Understanding: ChemForge will integrate information across diverse chemical representations---textual descriptions (literature, protocols), 2D molecular graphs, and 3D atomic structures. This holistic understanding enables deeper insights into chemical systems than possible with unimodal models, thereby advancing its chemical understanding abilities. 2) Autonomous Agentic Reasoning: Moving beyond static question-answering, ChemForge will be empowered with complex, multi-step reasoning and planning capabilities crucial for chemical discovery. It will be trained to execute tasks such as retrosynthesis planning, de novo design, hypothesis generation, and experimental procedure reflection, to enable autonomous and agentic scientific discovery. Ultimately, ChemForge will be provided as a powerful, open-source foundation model to the scientific community, serving as a versatile tool to understand chemical phenomena, generate novel hypotheses, perform multi-turn chemical design and synthesis planning, and significantly accelerate the discovery of new materials and therapeutics.

requestTitle: Large Foundation Model for Voice Synthesis
abstract: Interest in voice recognition has been renewed due to advances in large foundation models, thanks to improved sound classification and prediction. However, existing systems struggle with low-resource languages and noisy environments, as they are pre-trained on clean, monolingual datasets such as LibriSpeech. To address these challenges, we introduce VoiceForge, a synthetic speech generation framework using latent-space mixup to create diverse, linguistically coherent speaker data. We expect value-adding use cases for voice interfaces in defense, emergency response and multilingual settings, which generally consist limited training data. Preliminary results show superior outperformance over existing models, where we seek to scale up the model (named as VoiceForge) for a wider scope of adaptation.

requestTitle: Inferential Fine-Tuning (IFT) of Foundation Models using Step-by-Step Distillation Approach for Biomedical Drug Discovery Application
abstract: This project will develop an innovative fine-tuning framework for highly specialized biomedical LLM applications that can support inferencing over multi-modal data and accurately contextualize long-range dependencies in biomedical data. In contrast to existing approaches that use resource expensive data annotation pipelines to generate high quality training data, this project will leverage existing biomedical ontologies with automated reasoners to generate reliable training data for resource-efficient fine-tuning LLMs as part of a step-by-step distillation. This a promising new direction for rapid fine-tuning of LLMs in biomedical applications as compared to existing a rule-based, manually crafted approach, which addresses the issues of efficiency, scalability, and accuracy.

Large-Scale SNV Embeddings from GPT-3.5 for Genetic Analysis
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown promise in genomic analysis, but their application to large-scale genetics remains limited. We propose to generate GPT-3.5 embeddings for 8.9 billion single nucleotide variants (SNVs) by integrating functional annotations from FAVOR, clinical significance from ClinVar, and statistical associations from the GWAS Catalog. These embeddings will be publicly available and evaluated for downstream tasks such as hypothesis testing and phenotype prediction. Our approach aims to enhance genetic variant interpretation and provide a reusable resource for the broader research community.

requestTitle: Student Modeling in Open-ended Learning Activities
abstract: Student modeling is critical to personalization and teacher support in educational applications. Traditional student modeling approaches are limited to rigid, closed-form learning activities, such as students responding to practice/assessment questions. As more and more educational activities become interactive, partly powered by advances in generative artificial intelligence (AI), there is a need for student modeling in interactive, open-ended learning activities, such as interactive coding activities, tutor-student dialogues, and student sourcing activities in language learning. In this project, we will develop large language model (LLM)-based student models for student debugging behavior, textual student knowledge and error summarizations, and keyword mnemonics generation.

requestTitle: Collaborative Research: Conference: NAIRR Pilot Expansion: FA1: Utilizing NAIRR Pilot Resources for Building Sustainable Blue Economy
abstract: The Blue Economy includes research areas focused on the sustainable use of ocean resources for economic growth, including marine resource management, renewable ocean energy, sustainable fisheries and aquaculture, and maritime transportation. AI has transformative potential to enhance blue economy research by providing advanced tools for data analysis, modeling, and decision-making. For instance, AI can analyze data from sensors, satellites, and autonomous underwater vehicles to monitor ocean conditions, predict weather patterns, and assess ecosystem health in real-time. Machine learning algorithms can optimize sustainable fishing practices by analyzing fish stock data, helping to prevent overfishing while supporting local economies. The NSF has funded several AI and High-Performance Computing (HPC) systems to advance AI research across various scientific domains. One example is Texas A&M's AI/HPC cluster, Accelerated Computing for Emerging Sciences (ACES), an NSF NAIRR (National AI Research Resource) Pilot resource led by Co-PI Honggao Liu (Executive Director of High-Performance Research Computing at Texas A&M University (TAMU)), with PI Zhang (Assistant Professor of Geography, TAMU) serving as a Co-Investigator. In addition, Co-PI Sean Cleveland (Director of Cyberinfrastructure for the University of Hawaii System’s Information Technology Services Cyberinfrastructure group) serves as Co-PI for the NSF Jetstream2 Hawaii regional cloud instance (#2005506 another NAIRR Pilot resource). This workshop project aims to bring together scientists from three coastal regions - the Gulf of America, Maryland, and the Pacific Region (Hawaii) - to leverage NSF NAIRR pilot resources to advance AI-driven Blue Economy research. The workshop will include a panel discussion, student paper presentations, and an AI-driven NAIRR resources training session. This project will leverage PI Zhang's previous NSF-funded Convergence Accelerator - Networked Blue Economy project (#2137684), which established a broad collaborative network spanning organizations such as the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration Fisheries, the University of Texas at Austin, the National Center for Atmospheric Research, the University of California San Diego, and the Pacific Fishery Management Council.

requestTitle: ForenCaps: Advanced Capsule Networks for Audio Forensic Analysis
abstract:
As fake image and video technologies become more sophisticated, detecting deepfakes has become increasingly challenging. This project proposes a new AI-based approach to improve deepfake detection using a specialized neural network architecture called a capsule network. Our innovation integrates information-theoretic concepts, specifically entropy, into the model’s decision-making process to improve both accuracy and interpretability.

Unlike traditional methods that focus on surface-level textures, our approach captures deeper spatial relationships within images and videos, enabling more reliable detection of subtle manipulations. Preliminary results show improved detection performance on benchmark datasets. The project aims to scale this approach through extensive testing on diverse deepfake datasets using advanced computing resources provided by the NAIRR Pilot.

The outcomes of this work will contribute to building more transparent, trustworthy, and robust AI systems, and the resulting tools will be shared openly with the research community to support future innovation in digital media forensics.

requestTitle: Modeling Extended Sequential Data for Business Analytics
abstract: This proposal outlines a project to rigorously benchmark a novel automated modeling approach for lengthy sequential business data against state-of-the-art methods, leveraging NAIRR Pilot resources.

requestTitle: Continual Federated Unlearning for Large Language Models
abstract:
We propose a federated framework for on-demand unlearning in large language models (LLMs), enabling multiple clients to request the removal of undesirable knowledge from a shared LLM while preserving general utility without sharing sensitive unlearning data. Our research introduces two key innovations. First, we decouple unlearning from traditional reliance on both forgetting and retaining data, which is often impractical for external clients to
provide. Instead, we frame unlearning as a preference alignment task and allow clients to generate lightweight, private task vectors that can be efficiently merged on the server. Second, we develop a hierarchical federated aggregation method to integrate unlearning requests from heterogeneous clients, supporting scalable and efficient incorporation of new unlearning requests. To minimize the interference of unlearning with retained knowledge, we further align unlearning and retaining objectives in a shared space via subspace projection. Our research aims will jointly offer a dynamic, privacy-conscious solution for practical continual unlearning in LLMs.

requestTitle: VANGUARD: Variant Analysis and Next-Gen Updates for AI-enabled Rapid Diagnosis
abstract: VANGUARD (Variant Analysis and Next-Gen Updates for AI-enabled Rapid Diagnosis) builds on our 2021 work—clinically deployed and published in NEJM and Nature Biotechnology—which set a world record for the fastest genomic diagnosis using Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing. This project advances that pipeline to build a next-generation, AI-accelerated computational infrastructure for ultra-rapid genomic diagnosis in critical care. We propose adaptive basecalling using model-aware routing for basecalling, dynamic variant calling via a meta-model trained on genomic context, and developing learning-based triage systems for variant prioritization. The proposed system will reduce the manual review burden, and support broader clinical deployment. Aligned with NAIRR’s focus areas in AI for science, individual health, and edge-data workflows, VANGUARD exemplifies how AI and distributed systems can transform diagnostic genomics.

requestTitle: Consensus-Seeking Autonomous Agents in Complex Cyber-Physical Transportation Systems
abstract: Modern transportation systems are shaped by intricate interactions among diverse agents, including human drivers, vulnerable road users, automated vehicles (AVs), and infrastructure systems. These interactions are governed by divergent objectives, non-aligned incentives, and individualized behavioral preferences. As AVs become more common, the lack of shared understanding across agents presents a growing challenge, particularly in complex and dynamic traffic environments. This project proposes a framework for consensus-seeking architectures in cyber-physical transportation systems. The approach centers on modeling behavioral heterogeneity, training AI agents based on these diverse preferences, and evaluating the system-level implications of multi-agent interaction at scale.

requestTitle: An Efficient Text-to-SQL System for Automatic Database Querying using Constrained Decoding
abstract: What if we can develop an efficient Text-to-SQL (Text2SQL) system that is able to translate human language to SQL queries, so that humans can directly “talk to” databases? Motivated by our collaboration with the James City County Fire Department (JCCFD) in Virginia, this system will enable non-technical users, such as first responders and administrators, to retrieve critical data via natural language queries. By removing the technical barrier of SQL, the system contributes to advancements in societally-critical research. Specifically, it improves the reliability and efficiency of emergency response systems by enabling faster and more accurate data access for first stakeholders and decision-makers. Our goal is threefold: 1) we aim to develop an efficient Text2SQL system using the ideas of constrained decoding, among others, 2) we aim to deploy our methodology in the database system of our collaborator, JCCFD, to assist their daily operations and routing decision-making, 3) we aim to publish our findings in a research paper and open-source code repository.

requestTitle: Measuring Multi-sensory Place Perceptions using Multi-modal Diffusion Models
abstract: In this project, we aim to develop several cutting-edge multi-modal diffusion models to measure and understand human perceptions of places from multiple dimensions. In particular, we request computational resources to support the development two place-specific generative models Soundscape2Landscape and Landscape2Soundscape based on Diffusion models. To train these models, we will build three soundscape-to-image datasets based on SoundingEarth, street view images, and YouTube videos. These Diffusion-based models could link human auditory experiences and visual experiences at place, advancing our understanding of human-environment relationships, and benefit geography and urban studies.

Transforming Undergraduate Data Science Education Through Large Language Model Integration: STAT 4220 Predictive Analytics
abstract: This educational allocation enables 100 University of Pennsylvania undergraduate students to gain hands-on experience with transformer models (DistilBERT, BERT, BART/T5) through four homework assignments and a comprehensive final project in STAT 4220: Predictive Analytics with Python. Direct classroom observation with 90+ students revealed critical infrastructure gaps where personal laptops cannot handle 24+ hour AI computations, creating performance bottlenecks and educational inequity. This request for 915 GPU hours addresses documented needs while establishing a replicable model for LLM-enhanced statistics curricula nationwide. Students will execute real-world applications including financial sentiment analysis, business document classification, question answering, and text summarization, directly preparing them for AI-driven careers in fintech, consulting, and data science. The project demonstrates NAIRR's educational mission by democratizing access to cutting-edge AI tools while creating evidence-based best practices for undergraduate AI education.

requestTitle: Evaluating Human Engagement Classification in Human-Robot Interaction Using Pre-trained Open-Source Vision Language Models
abstract: In the context of human-robot interaction (HRI) it is important for robots to accurately perceive human engagement in order to respond appropriately. This work aims to evaluate open-source vision language models (VLMs) in modeling human engagement across two HRI applications: support group facilitation and conflict resolution practice. VLM size and performance trade-off will be assessed.

requestTitle: Deep Functional Charting and Encoding of the Developing Brain
abstract: The human brain undergoes profound remodeling from childhood to young adulthood, marking a sensitive period when many mental health and behavioral problems first emerge. Understanding functional maturation during this time is crucial for deciphering the neurobiological basis of cognition and behavior and for identifying developmental deviations linked to mental health disorders. Despite extensive efforts to document structural brain changes, precise whole-brain charting of functional development remains limited due to the small sample sizes of typical neuroimaging studies and the substantial noise in functional MRI, which complicates the accurate quantification of developmental trajectories. To address these challenges, this project will leverage advanced neuroinformatics and machine learning techniques to analyze large-scale resting-state fMRI data from individuals aged 6 to 25. We will (1) develop a foundation model to encode individualized functional fingerprints predictive of behavioral and mental health outcomes and (2) systematically chart functional neurodevelopment using these functional fingerprints to quantify developmental deviations linked to psychiatric vulnerability. By curating and harmonizing 19 publicly available neuroimaging datasets, encompassing 50,000 resting-state fMRI scans from over 30,000 individuals, we will create the most comprehensive resource to date for characterizing functional brain development and its relevance to psychological well-being. The resulting model has the potential to be used in clinical and research settings for early identification of neurodevelopmental vulnerabilities, personalized intervention strategies, and biomarker discovery.

requestTitle: Calibrating LLM Refusals for Trustworthy Mental Health Support
abstract: In the context of intelligent assistance for mental health support, over-refusal by large language models (LLMs) presents a critical challenge: when individuals seek help online for anxiety, depression, or other mental health concerns, unjustified refusals—even if safety-motivated—can lead to feelings of invalidation, abandonment, or distrust in digital care systems. This issue is compounded by the ambiguity and emotional nuance of user expressions in mental health contexts, where models must distinguish between genuine distress and policy-violating queries with care and precision. Existing LLMs often rely on rigid heuristics or oversimplified safety filters, leading to misaligned refusal behaviors at inference time. This project investigates the dynamics of refusal miscalibration in specialized mental health assistance scenarios and proposes a two-part solution: (1) the creation of domain-sensitive refusal benchmarks that include a wide range of emotionally charged, contextually ambiguous, and ethically sensitive user prompts—each annotated for ground truth refusal intent and safety relevance; and (2) the development of a lightweight, inference-time intervention module that inspects the model’s chain-of-thought reasoning and intermediate response drafts to determine whether a refusal or compliance decision is contextually appropriate, with the ability to override or enforce refusal as needed. This approach complements broader advances in user modeling and natural language generation by introducing a layer of behavioral safety auditing focused on real-time decision-making. By improving the alignment between model behavior and user needs in sensitive digital health environments, the proposed work aims to increase trust, mitigate harm, and enhance the effectiveness of AI-driven mental health support systems.

requestTitle: Building Open Source Dataset, Models, and RL Algorithms for GUI-based Reasoning Agents
abstract:
Recent advancements in large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable progress in structured reasoning tasks, particularly in mathematical domains. While these models excel at solving closed-form problems, their potential to assist humans in dynamic, real-world multimodal scenarios remains underexplored.
This research advances GUI automation by combining dataset construction, model development, and algorithmic advances. The outcomes includes open-source implementations, benchmark datasets, and state of the art  GUI agent models. Our work lays the foundation for next-generation autonomous digital assistants that understand, reason about, and interact with complex software ecosystems through natural language.

requestTitle: MergeBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Model Merging in Foundation Models
abstract: Model merging is an emerging research direction that offers an effective strategy to combine the strengths of multiple fine-tuned models into a unified model that preserves the specialized capabilities of each. It provides a flexible and efficient way to compose skills from different tasks, enabling continual learning and knowledge transfer, especially in the context of large-scale foundation models where training from scratch is prohibitively expensive. Despite the growing literature on model merging, there is a lack of systematic evaluation and comparison of model merging methods, especially in the context of foundation models. In this proposal, we introduce MergeBench, a comprehensive benchmark for model merging in foundation models. Our benchmark consists of a diverse set of tasks that cover a wide range of domains, including instruction-following, mathematics, multilingual understanding, coding, and safety. We evaluate eight model merging methods on a suite of tasks, including supervised fine-tuning and evaluation tasks, to provide a comprehensive comparison of their performance. Our benchmark will serve as a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners to evaluate and compare model merging methods, facilitating the development of more effective and efficient model merging algorithms. As a concrete application of our benchmark, we will investigate the effectiveness of model merging in safe information localization, and explore its use in improving the safety alignment of multi-lingual large language models (LLMs).

requestTitle: Start-Up: Shaojun Pei, Harvard University
Fully Transparent and Robust LLMs for Healthcare
abstract: The need for fully open science clinical LLMs to enable research into their capabilities and weaknesses (including biases), and to ultimately permit safe deployment for practical tasks is ever increasing. We hypothesize that, if carefully designed, domain-adapted LLMs can offer substantial benefits compared to generalist models. Existing clinical LLMs have fallen short, probably due to indiscriminate data selection and use of generic training objectives. Motivated by these findings, we propose to train and release a family of relatively small open science clinical LLM—all fine-tuned from the open science OLMo 2 model using a mix of curated data and domain-informed post-training objectives that we will open-source. We anticipate that these resources and methods will yield more accurate and robust clinical LLMs across a range of tasks. Such transparency is critical if we are to use LLMs in healthcare. Moreover, fully open clinical LLMs will permit new LLM science investigating domain adaptation and mechanistic interpretability.

requestTitle: Computational Approaches for Rapid Inhibition of Gene Editing Enzymes
abstract: We are developing computational approaches to rapidly design inhibitors of gene editing technologies, specifically CRISPR-Cas systems and other programmable nucleases. This work is being done with support of the DARPA RIDDL (Rapid Inhibitor Discovery and Development pipeLine) program, whose goal it is to develop the capability to identify inhibitor candidates with >99% potency and >90% specificity within 24 hours of encountering a novel gene editor, supporting critical biodefense capabilities. Our work on this project combines machine learning models for predicting peptide–protein interactions with large-scale experimental screening to create a pipeline that can design potent inhibitors for any arbitrary gene editor. A second aim is to develop classifiers that can predict the efficacy and safety of these novel inhibitors.

requestTitle: AI-Driven Methods for Discovering and Proving Mathematical Inequalities
abstract: Our project aligns with the NAIRR Pilot’s mission to democratize access to AI resources for advancing scientific discovery.  By developing an AI-driven framework that integrates large language models, reinforcement learning, and symbolic computation, we aim to contribute to the automation of the discovery and proof of mathematical inequalities. These inequalities are ubiquitous across various scientific and engineering disciplines. This initiative exemplifies the NAIRR Pilot’s objective to harness AI for accelerating science and discovery.

requestTitle: Toward Foundation Multi-Step Model Through Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Recent advances in supervised fine-tuning (SFT) of large language models (LLMs) have significantly improved their capabilities in a variety of natural language tasks. However, these models still face substantial challenges when tasks require multiple steps of reasoning, complex retrieval processes, and effective integration of external tools or resources. Such tasks, often referred to as multi-hop question answering or iterative reasoning, represent realistic scenarios encountered frequently in practical applications, yet they remain difficult for current LLM frameworks. In this pilot project, we propose a reinforcement learning (RL)-based approach to teach LLMs how to strategically orchestrate interactions with external resources, e.g., web search, code execution, and domain-specific knowledge bases, significantly improving their ability to handle complex, multi-step reasoning tasks.

requestTitle: AI-Powered Clinical Pharmacology: Enhancing Lifespan-Based Prescribing Through Interactive Learning
abstract: This project will develop and implement three 24/7 retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)-based conversational chatbots to support nurse practitioner students in mastering antimicrobial pharmacology—one of the most challenging and high-stakes areas in their advanced pharmacology course. Antimicrobial content accounts for 50% of a major exam in the course and this content is consistently associated with high stress, low performance, and increased risk of student withdrawal. The chatbots will be embedded into the course as an on-demand, interactive learning tool for the duration of the 16 weeks in the semester. The conversational chatbots will allow students to ask questions and get evidence-based rationale responses. The chatbots will mimics faculty guidance and will help address gaps in understanding, improve academic performance, and reduce the need for individualized tutoring in a fully online learning environment. This innovative approach aligns with national priorities in nursing education and antimicrobial stewardship and has the potential to scale across other complex content areas in healthcare education.

requestTitle: Novel Methods for Unlearning in Graph Neural Networks
abstract: With a recent increase in concern for privacy and data protection, several regulations have been passed to ensure the security of personal information in cyberspace. Prominent among these is the right to be forgotten, which allows individuals to request the complete erasure of their data from a system. Consequently, GNNs trained on data from such systems must be adjusted to comply with these legal mandates. Unlearning is also crucial for maintaining model robustness by removing the influence of outdated or malicious data. This task of eliminating the impact of certain training instances is referred to as Machine Unlearning. A simple yet legitimate solution is to retrain the GNN model from scratch with the unwanted instances deleted from the training set. However, in a production environment, this naive approach can be costly in terms of deployment time and computational resources. To address this problem, we will propose efficient unlearning techniques in this project.

requestTitle: Enhancing Privacy-Preserving LLM Pipelines: Expanding Benchmarks, Improving Local Model Performance, and Exploring Complex System Structures
abstract: This project investigates privacy-preserving methods for Large Language Model (LLM) applications, focusing on preventing the disclosure of Personally Identifiable Information (PII) to untrusted LLMs at inference time.  Building upon the previously developed PAPILLON pipeline, which leverages trusted but weaker local models to selectively utilize untrusted but powerful API-based models, this research aims to enhance the pipeline's capabilities and address limitations.  The project will involve expanding the existing PUPA benchmark dataset with synthetic data and additional real-world conversations, improving the performance of smaller local LLMs through techniques like Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), and exploring more complex system structures for handling intricate user requests.  Additionally, a user study will be conducted to investigate the discrepancies between human and LLM understandings of PII, contributing to better alignment between user expectations and model behavior
