requestTitle: Sustainability Modeling and Management for Heterogeneous AI Systems
abstract:
As we aim to advance the study of Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy AI, we must do so in a sustainable and efficient manner. The recent advent of Large Language Models has accelerated the need for the design of efficient and environmentally responsible AI systems. For example, GPT-3, which consumed over 500 tons of carbon during its training process alone (i.e., the equivalent of the average annual consumption of 100 cars). This trend is only accelerating, with just data centers projected to consume as much as 14% of U.S. energy consumption by 2030. Recent advancements in AI accelerators provide promise of workload acceleration, often touting high FLOP count, large memory bandwidth, or novel dataflow architectures. However, with the plethora of specialized non-GPU accelerators available today, researchers are often left wondering which is the optimal choice for their given workload. This poses a high barrier to entry – as it is often unknown how a given workload will perform on a novel system. A suboptimal selection could induce costly overheads, including a large sustainability footprint that could otherwise be avoided.

In response, we propose an integrated research plan with three vectors—carbon attribution, heterogeneous processor management, heterogeneous model management—that form a comprehensive approach to sustainable computing. First, power and carbon analysis estimates the environmental impact of artificial intelligence (AI), enabling intelligent decision-making when scheduling workloads and allocating resources. Second, provisioning heterogeneous processors allows a system to leverage diverse capabilities, matching computational tasks to the appropriate hardware to optimize performance and energy efficiency. Third, training heterogeneous AI models allows a system to perform computation judiciously, matching inference queries to the appropriate model to optimize accuracy and resource efficiency.

This project is a supplement to Carbon Connect, our NSF Expedition in Computing that is (i) developing carbon accounting strategies for computing technology; (ii) mitigating embodied carbon by re-thinking hardware design; (iii) reducing operational carbon by re-thinking systems management; and (iv) balancing the complex interplay between embodied versus operational carbon. This supplement through NAIRR will allow for the exploration of the performance, efficiency, and sustainability of diverse AI architectures and hardware platforms.

For example, GPT-3, which consumed over 500 tons of carbon during its training process alone (i.e., the equivalent of the average annual consumption of 100 cars). This trend is only accelerating, with just data centers projected to consume as much as 14% of U.S. energy consumption by 2030. Recent advancements in AI accelerators provide promise of workload acceleration, often touting high FLOP count, large memory bandwidth, or novel dataflow architectures. However, with the plethora of specialized non-GPU accelerators available today, researchers are often left wondering which is the optimal choice for their given workload. This poses a high barrier to entry – as it is often unknown how a given workload will perform on a novel system. A suboptimal selection could induce costly overheads, including a large sustainability footprint that could otherwise be avoided.

In response, we propose an integrated research plan with three vectors—carbon attribution, heterogeneous processor management, heterogeneous model management—that form a comprehensive approach to sustainable computing. First, power and carbon analysis estimates the environmental impact of artificial intelligence (AI), enabling intelligent decision-making when scheduling workloads and allocating resources. Second, provisioning heterogeneous processors allows a system to leverage diverse capabilities, matching computational tasks to the appropriate hardware to optimize performance and energy efficiency. Third, training heterogeneous AI models allows a system to perform computation judiciously, matching inference queries to the appropriate model to optimize accuracy and resource efficiency.

This project is a supplement to Carbon Connect, our NSF Expedition in Computing that is (i) developing carbon accounting strategies for computing technology; (ii) mitigating embodied carbon by re-thinking hardware design; (iii) reducing operational carbon by re-thinking systems management; and (iv) balancing the complex interplay between embodied versus operational carbon. This supplement through NAIRR will allow for the exploration of the performance, efficiency, and sustainability of diverse AI architectures and hardware platforms.

requestTitle: Precision Genomics: Decoding RNA Dynamics and Genotype-to-Phenotype Mechanisms to Empower Personalized Medicine
abstract: While machine learning tools have revolutionized protein structure prediction, understanding the non-coding regions of the genome remains a significant challenge. We propose to construct a precision genomic foundation model that captures RNA dynamics and predicts functional consequences of mutations. We hypothesize that a large language model, trained on comprehensive genomic and transcriptomic data spanning diverse tissues and individuals, will yield profound insights into RNA regulatory mechanisms and elucidate pathways through which genetic mutations contribute to disease development.

requestTitle: Accelerating Multidisciplinary Fluid Dynamics with Foundation Models
abstract:
Accelerating simulation is a crucial task for advancing science and engineering. Deep learning-based surrogate models have shown promise in this area, but to date, success has been limited to high-data regimes. We aim to build on our previous work on Multiple Physics Pretraining and utilizing a newly developed dataset titled “The Well” to extend these capabilities to low-data regimes. 

We introduce "the Well," a large-scale dataset for physical simulation, containing 15.6TB of diverse fluid-like simulations. With this new dataset, we aim to train the largest and most broadly applicable foundation model for fluid-like behavior to date. Our approach builds on previous work in Multiple Physics Pretraining, addressing current limitations in scale and pretraining diversity. We will evaluate the model's transfer capabilities using subtasks within the Well as downstream tasks. All data, code, and pretrained weights will be made publicly available. Given sufficient resources, we will also explore scaling laws in this domain, potentially accelerating the development of more powerful foundation models for scientific applications.

requestTitle: Using Scenario-Based Simulation to Optimize Policies that Mitigate Impacts of AI in Society
abstract: This project leverages LLMs to write, re-write, and evaluate textual scenarios describing the impacts of generative AI in society under different policy conditions which are themselves generated by LLMs with input from a participatory process. This method thus enables a policy simulation process which results in an output policy that optimally mitigates the societal impacts of a technology in society according to chosen metrics. A large number of tokens is needed to simulate and evaluate many variations of scenarios under different policy conditions in order to implement this method.

requestTitle: Sustainable Edge-Cloud Collaborative Computing Paradigm for Large-Scale AI Models with Privacy Preservation
abstract: Along with the development of artificial intelligence and the Internet of Things, various battery-driven Internet of Things (IoT) devices with limited computing capabilities, such as smartwatches and smartphones, have become promising in all aspects of human lives. The demand for Artificial Intelligence (AI) models, especially large-scale AI models, including large language models (LLMs) and large visual language models (LVLMs), deployed on IoT devices has significantly increased in various areas such as healthcare, daily companionship, and personal health assistance. However, in most scenarios, these large-scale AI models store user-gathered data in the cloud for training and operation on IoT devices, which can potentially lead to privacy leaks and significant energy consumption. To address these issues, we propose to convert the cloud-based LLMs and LVLMs into edge LLMs and LVLMs employing a sustainable edge-cloud collaborative computing paradigm which can not only share effective knowledge among various IoT devices without jeopardizing user privacy but also ensure the performance of large-scale AI models on various IoT devices in terms of energy efficiency and model accuracy.

requestTitle: Long-context Multi-modal I/O in Conversational AI via Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Advancements in large language models (LLMs) have significantly improved conversational AI, enabling more natural human-machine interactions. However, current models often fall short in long-context multi-modal reasoning, limiting their ability to integrate and respond coherently to both visual and textual information. To address these challenges, we propose a novel framework that utilizes retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) techniques to enhance long-context multi-modal input and output in conversational AI systems. Our approach includes: (1) a RAG-oriented vision-language fusion module for efficient information retrieval from extensive multi-modal databases based on user queries and images; (2) a mixture-of-experts (MoE) visual tokenization module that integrates features from multiple visual models using a meta-expert for optimal embedding; and (3) an LLM-based visual context reuse module that enables robust reasoning over extended multi-modal contexts by incorporating retrieved factual information into responses. This framework aims to enhance applications such as virtual assistants and customer support bots, enabling them to understand and respond to complex user inputs involving both text and images. By overcoming the limitations of existing models in multi-modal reasoning and long-context processing, our research seeks to improve user experience and broaden the applicability of conversational AI technologies.

requestTitle: Propaganda Detection through use of LLM
abstract: News outlets are widely recognized for their political affiliations, with many national platforms fostering biases to appeal to specific audiences. The journalists working for these outlets play a pivotal role in shaping the narratives they present. In this project, we aim to examine how journalists from prominent news organizations may contribute to the spread of bias through the use of propaganda-like language. We plan to evaluate a range of Large Language Models to detect propaganda in both news articles and social media microblogs. Additionally, we aim to develop a browser extension that integrates this technology to assist readers in analyzing the potential bias in the content they consume.

requestTitle: Data-Centric Medical Multimodal Large Language Models for Factual Medical Diagnosis
abstract: This proposal aims to develop data-centric medical multimodal large vision-language models (Med-LVLMs) to enhance factual accuracy in medical diagnoses. Current models struggle with hallucinations and incorrect medical analysis due to misalignment between multimodal data such as electronic health records and medical imaging. To address these challenges, the research focuses on three main aims: (1) generating and augmenting labeled preference data from unlabeled medical input using advanced techniques like response rewarding and model collaboration, (2) improving modality alignment through sample importance estimation by optimizing preference data based on quality, and (3) leveraging external knowledge to improve factual accuracy in rare medical abnormalities using calibrated retrieval and balanced knowledge utilization. The proposal involves a multidisciplinary team with extensive experience in machine learning, healthcare, and medical imaging. The outcomes will be shared via publications, open-source tools, and collaborations with medical institutions, contributing to the development of reliable AI systems in healthcare.

requestTitle: DCL 24-093 NAIRR Demonstration Project: A National Hydrology AI Digital Twin Pilot
abstract: Fresh water is central to human civilization and the health of all terrestrial ecosystems, yet our ability to quantify and predict it is primitive at best.  We are facing a water future that will be more uncertain and more extreme than the past. Existing tools are not evolving fast enough to address these challenges. 99% of liquid freshwater is stored underground. Groundwater supports half the global population, 60% crop production and ecosystems, yet it is so sparsely observed that it cannot be simulated with data driven statistical or machine learning approaches. Our team is building the first high resolution hydrologic digital twin for the US that extends from the bedrock to the treetops.  Using a hybrid machine learning approach, we are able to maintain close fidelity to the most physically rigorous modeling platforms available  . This platform  will create an unprecedented ability to explore parts of the hydrologic cycle that are too sparsely observed to fit traditional data driven machine learning models to.    Our pilot will be to develop an operational digital twin which can generate monthly national forecasts in real time each day. All outputs will be publicly hosted and freely accessible.

requestTitle: NAIRR: CCSS: Modeling and Learning Space-time Structures for Real-time Environment Perception
abstract: Developing sensing circuits and systems capable of perceiving the physical environment is an essential step toward next-generation cyber-physical systems that leverage computation, communication, and sensing integrated with the physical domain. The recent introduction of a class of artificial intelligence (AI) methods known as deep learning has drastically advanced vision-based environment perception. However, the applicability of these methods is significantly limited by their reliance on vast amounts of 3D annotations for training, which are expensive, unnatural, and often unobtainable. Acquiring 3D annotations necessitates specialized data captured by 3D sensors rather than utilizing abundant and readily available images or videos. Moreover, it requires a controlled environment or compromises with inaccurate subjective labeling. This project aims to address real-time environment perception in a very challenging, largely unexplored, yet highly practical setting, where only 2D annotations are available during training, by modeling and learning rich space-time structures of the environment. The outcomes of this project will significantly impact cyber-physical systems and facilitate a wide range of applications, from robots in manufacturing and personal services to autonomous vehicles that enhance people's mobility and safety. Furthermore, this project will tightly integrate research and education at the University of Illinois Chicago (UIC), which is a Minority Serving Institution (MSI), through curriculum development, research training for high school, undergraduate, and graduate students, broadening the participation of female and minority students, and community outreach.

requestTitle: Toward Efficient and Robust Dynamic Scene Understanding Based on Visual Correspondences
abstract: Finding correspondences is a fundamental problem in computer vision; visual correspondences provide useful cues for a machine to understand its dynamic surroundings in a manner similar to what humans do. For instance, as an agent moves around, it may learn that objects that are far away like mountains typically do not move much, whereas nearby buildings and bushes appear to move rapidly in the environments as the agent changes position relative to them. Although significant advances have been made in solving various forms of visual correspondence problems, different correspondence models maintain different designs despite their inherent similarity, making the effective design principles and the learned representations difficult to transfer from one problem to another. In response to this challenge, this project aims to solve disparate visual correspondence problems with a unified model.

requestTitle: Assessing Accountability of Socio-Critical Software Systems
abstract:
The growth of big data and advancements in AI have empowered software to address complex, evolving challenges within socio-economic and legal domains. However, the increasing dependence on such software raises critical questions regarding accountability in applications that carry legal and social significance. This project aims to ensure accountability in software handling socio-legal implications, focusing on the legal, social, and ethical expectations for fairness, legal compliance, and user privacy.

Key challenges arise from the absence of formal behavioral specifications in legal-critical applications, such as tax software, which are complicated further by the U.S. legal system’s reliance on precedent (stare decisis). To address these challenges, we propose that accountability requirements can be viewed as metamorphic relationships, reflecting similarities across cases in specific contexts. The project has three primary objectives: 1) Explication of Metamorphic Relations, 2) Ensuring Fairness and Procedural Justice, and 3) Development of Accountability Artifacts: The project will create resources and artifacts to measure the accountability of software as it evolves over time.

Achieving these goals requires substantial computational resources to analyze large-scale legal and social datasets, train robust AI models, and conduct extensive simulations for compliance testing and fairness verification. We seek support for these computing resources to further our mission of building accountable and fair software systems for societal benefit.

requestTitle: PRIME: A Foundational Predictive Real-time Intersection Monitoring Engine
abstract:
Traffic intersections remain critical points of vulnerability in transportation infrastructure, accounting for 20% of vehicular accidents and over 7,000 annual fatalities in the United States. Current intersection monitoring systems, relying on basic motion detection or single-class object detection, struggle with complex scenarios involving multiple road users and varying environmental conditions. This research proposes PRIME (Predictive Real-time Intersection Monitoring Engine), a foundational traffic intersection monitoring algorithm that integrates advanced deep learning techniques for multi-class video object detection and trajectory prediction.
This project directly aligns with NAIRR priority areas by creating open-source foundation models for specific applications and utilizing experimental data from sensors and detectors. The proposed system employs a modified YOLOv8 architecture enhanced with feature pyramid networks and combines transformer encoders with graph neural networks to achieve robust object detection and accurate 5-second trajectory predictions. Our technical objectives include developing a multi-class detection system with over 95% accuracy, implementing proactive trajectory prediction, and generating anonymous traffic patterns for urban planning.
The project will be executed within twelve months, utilizing TACC Frontera GPU resources for model development and training. We will also release our codebase and make our annotated dataset publicly available with the aim of establishing a common foundation for intersection monitoring systems, enabling transfer learning and facilitating the development of more sophisticated safety solutions for smart transportation infrastructure.

requestTitle: Foundation Models for Spatio-temporal and Multi-modal Geospatial Data
abstract: Geospatial imagery data, collected by diverse satellite-based sensors over time, offers immense potential for enabling a wide range of high-impact applications, including climate change monitoring, precision agriculture, and natural disaster response. This potential stems from the rich, contextualized information provided across multiple channels and sensing modalities, spanning extended temporal ranges. As machine learning technologies advance, their application to geospatial data analysis becomes increasingly crucial for addressing critical environmental and sustainability challenges. However, existing foundation models cannot effectively handle the unique characteristics of spatio-temporal and multi-modal geospatial data, limiting their effectiveness in these vital applications. This proposal presents a comprehensive plan to design, analyze and evaluate large-scale foundation models specifically tailored for multi-modal and sptio-temporal geospatial data. Our research aims to overcome three key bottlenecks: (a) enable large-scale pre-training by significantly reducing the need for labeled geospatial data, (b) design novel foundational model architectures for geospatial data analysis, and (c) develop downstream applications to monitor environmental impacts of industrial activities at scale. We propose innovative techniques for multi-modal and hyperspectral pre-training, leveraging the intrinsic spatial and spectral interrelationships of geospatial data. This framework is further extended to accommodate spatio-temporal geospatial data, enabling comprehensive analysis across both space, channel, and time dimensions. Our work will advance the state-of-the-art in geospatial data analysis, contributing to the development of new tools for understanding and improving environmental outcomes from industrial activities.

requestTitle: Humanoid Robotics for Advanced Farming Automation
abstract: The objective of the research is to develop an AI driven 3D humanoid robotics posture control and the 3D spatial learning large language model to advance farming automation to improve national food security. 3D humanoid robot posture control robot will be developed through a large-scale video understanding. The 3D humanoid robot posture control will enable the humanoid robot to walk on the uneven farming environment smoothly. The 3D spatial learning large language model developed from the research will enable the humanoid robot to perform multiple on farm tasks. The 3D spatial learning will allow the humanoid robot to interact with farming equipment and tools fluently thus to accomplish various on farm tasks. Multiple on farm tasks range from harvesting of fruits and vegetables to the spray of chemicals on fruits and vegetable to control weed and pest will be implemented through the research. It is expected that the research will contribute to the improvement national food security.

requestTitle: Pixel Perfect: Decoding Generative Modelling Gaps in Medical Imaging
abstract: Modern image generation techniques can learn to produce images of a specified type (e.g., mammogram, lung x-ray and so on) from random inputs. If these image generators were accurate, they would be extremely useful. For example, an accurate image generator could act as a prior to allow image capture at low radiation levels. However, there is good evidence that generated images can be distinguished from real images quite easily. This proposal describes research intended to improve the accuracy of generated medical images.

requestTitle: Privacy-Preserving Generative AI for Synthetic Mobility Data Generation
abstract:
Mobility data collected by ubiquitous sensors (e.g., GPS, cellphone, smartcard, Wi-Fi) have the potential for significant scientific and societal impacts. Especially in the era of AI, accessing large-scale mobility data plays a pivotal role in advancing research and benefiting society. 
However, most of these mobility data are often proprietary and thus cannot be accessed or costly to acquire by the research community unless released by data owners. Although some data owners are willing to share their mobility data with the public to unlock their values, but the sensitive nature of mobility data and unknown data privacy risks prevent them from doing so. In this project, we plan to advance existing data generation methods by designing innovative privacy-preserving generative AI models for large-scale multi-modal mobility data generation. We will consider different privacy-enhancing technologies such as differential privacy (DP) and different generative AI paradigms like diffusion models and LLMs. The final goal of this project is to release a privacy-preserving mobility data generation framework and share synthetic while realistic multi-modal mobility data for scientific and societal impacts.

requestTitle: A volumetric foundation model for brain imaging
abstract: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) data contains detailed millimeter-resolution three-dimensional information about the human brain. We propose to build and release an open, freely available volumetric Foundation Model for MRI-based neuroscience research. We will capitalize on a wealth of openly-available neuroimaging data to train a volumetric vision transformer model on a dataset of more than 140k scans. We will evaluate the model on disparate tasks, demonstrating that the model can be specialized to a variety of downstream use-cases. By openly releasing the model for use by the research community, we will advance the field broadly.

requestTitle: Improving Fairness in Detecting AI-Synthesized Fake Multimedia
abstract: DeepFake, a term increasingly mentioned in the news and social media, refers to highly realistic fake images, and videos created using AI algorithms.  Combating DeepFake technology requires a comprehensive strategy that extends well beyond the realm of mere detection, emphasizing the responsible design, development, and deployment of technologies. This also known as responsible forensics, focuses on applying forensic science to digital content ethically, ensuring that actions to identify and mitigate DeepFakes meet high ethical standards and respect for human rights. At the heart of responsible forensics lies the commitment to fairness, especially important in the context of generative AI. It is crucial for detection tools to be crafted and used in ways that prevent unintentional bias against certain individuals or groups, thus upholding justice and equality in the digital realm.  Therefore, our goal is to improve fairness in detecting novel DeepFakes, aligning with NAIRR's focus area on advancing "Advancing AI methods that enable scientific discovery'' and the core research aim on "Accelerating societally-relevant research on AI safety, reliability, security, and privacy.''

requestTitle: Development of AI Data-driven Models and Very Large Ensembles for the Prediction of Atmospheric Rivers and Extreme Weather Events
abstract: Atmospheric river (AR) storms landfalling on the West coast of North America from the Pacific play a pivotal role in global moisture transport, and can be beneficial when replenishing water supply or mitigating wildfire risks, as well as damaging when they are associated with severe hazards like extreme winds, flooding, and debris flows, which can result in significant damages to infrastructure, properties, and lives. We are requesting NAIRR Pilot Resources to develop high-resolution (at 2 and 6 km spatial resolution) data-driven AI weather forecast models to significantly improve the predictions of ARs and associated extreme weather events. For reference, the current operational weather prediction systems (in the US and Europe) are run at 9 and 18 km resolution with only 31 to 51 ensemble members and require several hours and immense computational resources to be executed. In contrast, the proposed AI weather models, once trained, will generate a forecast in just a few seconds to minutes allowing the development of very large ensembles (>7000 members), both regionally and globally.

requestTitle: Leveraging Machine Learned Interatomic Potentials to Predict Materials Synthesis Routes
abstract:
New materials are constantly sought to enable transformations in sustainable energy generation and storage, microelectronics, catalysis, and other applications. However, the experimental discovery of new solid phases and materials synthesis routes continues to be driven by slow, inefficient trial and error, with few guiding design rules.
	This project aims to robustly predict the mechanisms of solid-state reactions and identify promising routes to form target phases by leveraging machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) and chemical reaction networks (CRNs). MLIPs learn the relationship between material structure and thermodynamic properties. Training on datasets of bulk materials and materials interfaces, we will leverage MLIPs to simulate solid-state reactions. Through these simulations, we will assess the thermodynamics and kinetics of nucleation and growth, with reaction products identified automatically through unsupervised phase classification.
	By compiling the intermediates, products, and properties of many reactions, we will construct CRNs describing overall materials synthesis processes. These CRNs can be used to rationalize observed competition, including disordered products and impurity phases, with direct validation against in situ experimental characterization.
	This proposal represents a novel direction for machine learning and artificial intelligence in chemical and materials research, with the possibility to improve materials manufacturing and accelerate research into environmentally sustainable technologies.

requestTitle: Differentially Private LLMs via Distillation
abstract: We propose a novel approach for building privacy-preserving language models, based on a 3-step process involving differentially private fine-tuning and model distillation. Our preliminary results indicate that our approach can produce high-quality differentially private models and also reduce hallucinations in some cases. We request approximately 300,000 GPU-hours to support training models for our experiments in this project.

requestTitle: Aligning AI models for scientific simulations under a physics-informed framework
abstract: We have currently seen impressive gains in generative AI in the realm of text and image modeling, with tools such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Stable Diffusion, etc. However, the scale and performance of AI-based models in scientific domains have not yet reached such heights. To do so requires modeling scientific processes that occur at multiple scales or resolutions, which traditional neural networks are ill-suited to do. The PI has been developing neural operators to learn phenomena at any resolution, meaning they learn mappings between function spaces. However, an outstanding question is how to ensure that the AI models are trustworthy in real-world applications. We will incorporate physics-informed frameworks to ensure the alignment of these AI models in scientific domains. If awarded, the NAIRR resources will be utilized to train and align foundation models with neural operators that will learn to solve multiple systems of PDEs as well as multi-physics PDEs.

abstract: This research aims to enhance the capacity of multi-modal AI video understanding models to generate high-quality video descriptions tailored to the needs of Blind and Low Vision individuals. Our approach involves expanding the model's architecture, increasing attention heads and context windows, and augmenting the dataset to overcome current limitations. By doing so, we aim to surpass the current state of the art in AI-generated video descriptions, significantly improving their quality and accuracy.

requestTitle: Child-LLM Alignment from Language and Content Viewpoints
abstract: Gathering data from young children is essential for research on child development, but is is a slow and expensive process.  This project explores how to use Large Language Models in the design of the experiments design, and the analysis of the data. The objective is not to replace children but to use LLMs as a tool to increase research efficiency.  In addition to using LLMs to suggest improvements in the experiment design, we will assess their ability to predict the children's behaviors and mimic children's verbal responses.

requestTitle: Machine-learned particle-flow reconstruction
abstract: At the CERN Large Hadron Collider, protons collide at nearly the speed of light 40 million times per second, resulting in a large number of outgoing particles and up to petabytes of data per year. By studying the produced particles, we can better understand the laws of physics and potentially discover new particles or interactions. Reconstructing these particles in every collision is a computationally demanding task that can be tackled with machine learning. The goal of this project is to develop new computationally efficient machine learning algorithms to reconstruct particles in the current and next generation of particle colliders.

requestTitle: Advancing AI Research in Time Series Sensor Data Analysis
abstract:
This research project aims to advance the field of time series sensor data analysis by developing and evaluating innovative AI methodologies. The project addresses key challenges such as data scarcity, model robustness, and effective temporal pattern recognition through the following objectives:

1. Generative AI Models: Development of generative AI models to create synthetic data samples, mitigating issues related to data scarcity.
2. Embedding Techniques: Implementation of methods for embedding multivariate time series into a common feature space, enhancing model performance and interoperability.
3. Time Series Augmentation and Positional Encoding: Investigation of various time series augmentation techniques to improve model robustness and generalization and positional encoding methods to effectively capture temporal patterns in time series data.
4. Interpretability: Development of methods for deep learning interpretability in time series.

The project will utilize substantial GPU computational resources, and will leverage publicly available datasets such as the UCR Time Series Classification Archive and the MIMIC-III clinical database. The research outcomes will be disseminated through high-impact journal publications, conference presentations, open-source software releases, and workshops.

By addressing these critical areas, this project aims to contribute significantly to the advancement of AI methods for analyzing time series sensor data, ultimately facilitating practical applications in smart health and pervasive computing.

requestTitle: Enhancing Behavioral Analysis in Minecraft through AI Integration
abstract: Our project aims to improve how we study human thinking and problem-solving using the virtual world of Minecraft. We are developing a smart AI agent that can learn and perform tasks in Minecraft just like human players. This AI will help us understand complex behaviors by comparing its performance to humans playing the same game. By programming the AI with human-like limits, we can see how it handles different challenges and what strategies it uses. This research will create new ways to evaluate human cognition and help design better tools for personalized learning and training in the future.

requestTitle: Smart Cyberinfrastructure for Democratized Digital Agriculture over the Cloud
abstract:
The Intelligent Cyberinfrastructure with Computational Learning in the Environment (ICICLE) Institute, spearheaded by Ohio State University, seeks to democratize artificial intelligence (AI) and enhance its accessibility for societies and the scientific community. A key objective of ICICLE is to enable domain experts across diverse fields—including Digital Agriculture, Animal Ecology, and Material Science—to leverage AI for their research and scientific experiments effortlessly.

As part of ICICLE’s initiative to democratize AI, we are developing a comprehensive end-to-end pipeline tailored for Agronomists and Digital Agriculture experts. This pipeline will enable users to preprocess data efficiently, train deep learning models for tasks such as classification and regression, perform real-time data inference, visualize results, and deploy models on edge devices. 

Every stage in the pipeline requires GPUs for parallel/distributed computations, a secure storage system to fetch and save data, and efficient communication/networking mechanisms to ensure that data is transferred seamlessly from the storage space to the computing space. Given the data's substantial size and the models' complexity, leveraging GPUs and cloud computing resources is essential to ensure efficient training and deployment.

requestTitle: Enhancing Awareness and Addressing Algorithmic Bias in Machine Learning
abstract: Our project aims to raise awareness about algorithmic bias, provide strategies for its detection and mitigation, and facilitate equity in health research through an interactive platform. Specifically, we seek to assist researchers in identifying and minimizing algorithmic biases by providing them with a feedback tool addressing fairness concerns during the research process. This will promote ethical and responsible AI usage and improve transparency within healthcare research. Our specific aim is to develop a customized chatbot to raise awareness about algorithmic bias and enhance researchers’ knowledge about algorithmic fairness by providing a personalized support tool to facilitate the detection and mitigation of biases in ML for health research.

requestTitle: Improved LLM Alignment from Human Preferences via Social Choice Theory
abstract: The method of choice for aligning LLMs is via algorithms such as reinforcement learning with human feedback (RLHF). However, the expenses involved in acquiring high-quality human preference rankings has been major bottlenecks for academic research, and prevented the exploration of new algorithms for practical LLM alignment. Recent advances in synthetic data generation have made the acquisition of such data with limited human oversight much more feasible than in the past. Our project seeks to investigate novel strategies for synthetic data generation using open-source LLMs, develop new algorithms for social choice-based alignment, and ultimately make LLM alignment techniques more steerable, interpretable, and fair.

requestTitle: Flexible Robot Learning to realize Assistive Robots in Healthcare Facilities
abstract: The scientific goal for this project is to develop few-shot reinforcement learning algorithms that can learn long-horizon, dexterous mobile manipulation tasks using minimal human inputs and environment interactions. Our work is motivated by the pressing need faced by the healthcare sector. Due to the United States' aging population, increasing long-term care needs, and rising patient-to-nurse ratios, healthcare systems are being stretched thin. These pressures contribute to nurse burnout and can lead to diminished quality of care, resulting in a higher rate of patient readmissions. To ease the burden on the care staff, our team at the University of Maryland is developing an assistive robot, designed to aid with routine patient-facing and non-patient facing tasks. This robot can thus give back the time to the care staff, thereby allowing them to care for more patients and improving the quality of care. Towards this end, we are developing three specific robot learning pipelines that can learn assistive tasks with minimal human inputs, especially from non-robotics experts. The pipelines are aimed at minimizing the actual real-world interaction required in reinforcement learning to learn robust policies by leveraging the concept of solution sketches, and bootstrapping learning from demonstrations.

requestTitle: Improved Visual Text Rendering with Diffusion Models
abstract:
Diffusion models are the current state-of-the-art in prompt-based image generation, capable of creating novel images by inverting a training process that makes diffusive paths from data to noise. Research on improving their efficiency, scalability, and ability to process high-dimensional video data has been a major focus of the AI community.

We propose to address the challenge of visual text generation, an area where even state-of-the-art models have struggled to generate accurate or even legible glyphs corresponding to instructions in the prompt. There is a significant gap in this field in terms of constraint-free, flexible rendering of text and the incorporation of styles and context in the generated images. The work and the source codes as a result of this grant will be made open source.

requestTitle: Multimodal Conversational AI for Smart Geriatric Nursing
abstract: We aim to design, develop, and deploy a task-oriented multimodal conversational assistant to help older adults with their daily tasks. Our system facilitates daily tasks spanning diverse scenarios such as helping with online grocery shopping, recommending cooking recipes, home maintenance and improvement, and managing smart home devices. We will develop an Al-powered conversational assistant for older adult care by leveraging emerging technologies in Generative Al, NLP, and LLMs, which greatly promotes the life quality of older adults by improving their well-being, efficiency, safety, and independence. Our system will be widely adopted to promote healthy aging and living experience for a diverse spectrum of older Americans including those living in their homes independently, those receiving clinical care or skilled home and community-based services, and rural, underserved, and disabled populations.

requestTitle: Private Parameter Tuning with Large Language Models
abstract:
This project addresses hyperparameter tuning when training differentially private (DP) mechanisms, specifically DP data synthesizers, which is a fundamental challenge in this space. Hyperparameter tuning is challenging because we cannot tune a DP mechanism fit to our data sample by re-exposing the data over multiple parameter setting iterations without incurring additional (potentially substantial) privacy costs. Recent work has noted this challenge and, in particular, the potential for ``dishonesty'' in parameter tuning, to have serious and negative side effects, including risking privacy or overstating a DP mechanism's performance. A common narrative that attempts to circumvent this limitation assumes access to a publicly available sample for the protected dataset that can be used for tuning a mechanism. However, public data may not be readily available.

We seek to address the lack of available public data by leveraging large language models (LLMs) to generate realistic synthetic data to be used in place of real data for hyperparameter tuning. Our approach is to extensively benchmark state-of-the-art DP data synthesizers on different datasets, comparing hyperparameter tuning that uses LLMs with tuning that makes the public data assumption, alongside some reasonable baselines.

requestTitle: classification of suturing using video analysis
abstract:
Introduction:
Accurate and objective assessment of surgeons’ operative skills is essential for improving patient safety and quality of surgery. Recent advances in machine learning have enabled more automated skill assessments, particularly in minimally invasive and robotic surgeries, replacing traditional methods of evaluation that were limited by subjectivity and reproducibility. However, its application in open surgery has not advanced at a comparable rate and remains underdeveloped. In the present study, we aim to bridge this gap by employing a novel machine learning model, VisionSuture, to evaluate technical performance of surgical video recordings.

Methods:
The AIxSuture dataset, comprising 314 videos approximately 5 minutes each, taken at 30 frames per second, was utilized for this study. The dataset includes a global rating score (GBS) for each video, categorizing individuals into three classes: novice (n=119), intermediate (n=79), and proficient (n=116). Hybrid Convolutional Neural Network and Long-Short-Term-Memory (H-CNN-LSTM) networks were employed to train the video classifier model (Image 1A). ResNet50, a publicly available image classification model, served as a spatial feature extractor to perform non-linear transformations. Due to domain discrepancies between the AIxSuture dataset and ResNet50, this model was first fine-tuned on a subset of frames from the AIxSuture dataset. Conversely, LSTM networks captured the long-term temporal dependencies between feature maps (frames). This network primarily focused on retaining or discarding significant and insignificant scenes that demonstrate the suturing abilities of the subjects. To assess and compare the model's performance against existing models, the class-wise F1 score was used as the metric, chosen for its ability to provide an unbiased assessment in classification problems with imbalanced class distributions.

Results:
The architecture of the VisionSuture model is illustrated in Image 1A. Across the entire dataset analyzed, the VisionSuture model achieved an average F1 score of 80.1% in determining the performance level of each subject, outperforming previous models (Image 1B). Additionally, the model classified performance with up to 90.1% accuracy for the novice group, 65.7% for the intermediate group and 86.3% for the proficient group. Although VisionSuture predicted the intermediate cohort with lower accuracy than other skill levels, it outperformed other models in this group by at least 10% (Image 1B).

Conclusion:
The VisionSuture model provides a robust framework for skill assessment in open surgery. The application of machine learning in clinical practice should be considered to evaluate surgeons’ skills and help improve training and outcomes.

requestTitle: A Scalable Intellectual Property Safeguard for Large Language Models
abstract:
The goal of this project is to develop a scalable computational safeguard for potential intellectual property (IP) concerns raised in the use of large language models (LLMs). LLMs have transformed numerous real-world tasks and the broader landscape of AI, offering unprecedented opportunities for innovation. Particularly, LLMs demonstrate remarkable capacity for memorizing and “regurgitating” training data. Moreover, these models internalize vast amounts of world knowledge from their training
data. In the near future, LLMs are expected to perform derivative creativity, which involves using existing ideas, concepts, or creations as a foundation or inspiration to generate new, original works.

This research aims to address the complex interplay between LLMs and IP rights at multiple levels, including copyrighted material, proprietary knowledge, and creativity. By creating a robust and adaptable system, we seek to mitigate risks of IP infringement while fostering innovation in AI development. The significance of this research lies in its potential to establish ethical guidelines and practical tools for the responsible use of LLMs, balancing technological advancement with the protection of intellectual assets.
resourceName: DOE Argonne National Laboratory AI Testbed

requestTitle: AI for Infrastructure Resilience: Using Language to Predict Actions and Impacts in International Disputes
abstract: We use large language models (LLMs) to analyze the language preceding international disputes and predict the impacts of these disputes. By linking rhetoric to economic actions, we intend to develop predictive models to forecast international conflicts, which will help mitigate risks and strengthen infrastructure resilience. The project will create open-source tools and share them with scholars, policymakers, and executives, bridging the gap between AI technologies and practical applications. The feasibility of this approach has been tested using a case study of the China-Lithuania dispute, analyzing rhetoric changes and economic impacts.

abstract: Recent advancements in gene function prediction using machine learning and deep learning have shown promise. However, most methods rely on predefined labels or GO terms and focus on individual data modalities like protein sequence or structure, without integrating them. We propose a comprehensive approach that combines datasets including protein sequences, AlphaFold structures, and interaction networks to enhance gene function description. By leveraging the GPT-4 API, we aim to generate more accurate and interactive protein function descriptions, especially for uncharacterized genes.

requestTitle: Foundation Models for Advanced Cybermanufacturing
abstract:
This NAIRR Pilot project aims to revolutionize the manufacturing industry through the development of G-Forge, a multimodal AI-powered smart service. Led by researchers from Iowa State University and New York University, the project will leverage Large Language Models (LLMs) to create advanced tools for design, evaluation, and diagnostics in manufacturing processes.
G-Forge will focus on comprehending, debugging, and manipulating G-Code, the language used to control computer-aided manufacturing machines. The project aims to create a community-driven G-Code database, develop AI-powered verification and debugging tools, and enable G-Code analysis as a service. By democratizing access to sophisticated manufacturing tools, G-Forge has the potential to enhance innovation, efficiency, and resilience across the manufacturing sector, particularly benefiting small and medium-scale manufacturers.
This transformative project envisions laying the foundation for a 'Google for Manufacturing', fostering widespread adoption of advanced technologies and driving progress in both AI and secure digital manufacturing.

requestTitle: Multi-Modal Scientific Claim Verification
abstract: The advancements in large and multi-modal generative AI models have significantly expanded their capability to generate scientific claims across various applications and scenarios. However, due to outdated or incomplete information in their training datasets or hallucinations, these models still can produce incorrect scientific claims, causing great concerns. Existing solutions often only use textual evidence to verify such scientific claims which is limiting. In this project, instead, we propose to exploit multi-modal and contextual evidence, including bar charts, line graphs, tables in related and cited scientific papers, for comprehensive fact-checking of scientific claims. Our goal is to extend our prior efforts to larger, more comprehensive datasets across various domains (e.g., AI and material science) and modalities (e.g., texts, images, and citation graphs). This will involve developing a unified multi-modal framework to thoroughly verify scientific claims. Achieving this objective will, however, require extensive GPU resources for pre-training and fine-tuning the multi-modal architecture, which is the reason that we seek for help from the NAIRR pilot program.

requestTitle: Privacy in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract:
Trustworthy machine learning is critical to ensuring that AI systems can be safely and reliably deployed in real-world applications. This concept encompasses various aspects, including privacy and security, which are crucial in protecting sensitive data and maintaining trust in AI technologies. Generative models, particularly large language models (LLMs), have emerged as powerful tools for a wide range of tasks, from natural language processing to multimodal generation. However, current LLMs face issues such as hallucination, where the models generate incorrect or misleading information. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a promising solution to mitigate such problems by retrieving relevant documents and incorporating them into the generation process, enhancing the accuracy and reliability of the generated content. Despite its benefits, RAG systems raise significant privacy and security concerns, especially in scenarios where sensitive information may be exposed.

RAG works by retrieving documents from external sources, which are then used to augment the LLM's generation process. In applications like medical data analysis, the documents retrieved could contain sensitive or private information, making the privacy of these systems a pressing issue. In this project, we aim to investigate the privacy risks associated with RAG systems, such as the extraction of private documents, and propose a new privacy-preserving approach to mitigate these risks. The project will focus on two phases: first, identifying and analyzing potential privacy threats in RAG systems, including private document extraction attacks, under realistic scenarios; and second, exploring privacy-preserving techniques, such as differential privacy, to safeguard sensitive information in these systems.

To achieve our goals, we will conduct several experiments across both phases of the project. In the first phase, we will simulate RAG systems assuming the use of state-of-the-art LLMs, such as GPT-4 or GPT-4.0, to explore the extent of privacy vulnerabilities. In the second phase, we will continue testing these models while introducing multimodal RAG systems, which incorporate images as inputs, requiring us to generate synthetic image data using tools like DALL·E 3. Additionally, we will use embedding models to better understand the relationships between the inputs and outputs of these systems. These experiments will help us evaluate the potential risks and effectiveness of privacy-preserving techniques in both text- and image-based RAG systems.

requestTitle: Advancing Colorectal Cancer Diagnosis: A Multimodal AI Copilot for Real-Time Endoscopy
abstract: While AI has the potential to enhance diagnostic accuracy in endoscopy, current models fail to fully integrate natural language processing (NLP), limiting real-time doctor-AI interactions. We propose the development of EndoPilot, a multimodal AI copilot designed to assist clinicians during endoscopy by analyzing live footage, providing immediate assessments of polyps, and suggesting potential diagnoses. By aligning visual embeddings from endoscopy images with text from pathology reports, EndoPilot will improve diagnostic accuracy, reduce variability, and enable continuous AI learning from real-time data. Utilizing a vast dataset of over 5 million endoscopy images and corresponding reports, our multidisciplinary team aims to create an AI tool that advances cancer treatment and contributes to open-source clinical AI models.

requestTitle: Advancing Code Generation Safety with Large Language Models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have brought ground-breaking changes to code generation tasks and emerged as powerful tools transforming the landscape of software development. Despite their impressive performance and vast potential, these models have also raised significant safety concerns, preventing us from reliably deploying them in real-world applications. To be more specific, first, they could be abused to intentionally generate malicious or harmful code such as malware, ransomware, or backdoors. These models can lower the technical barrier for creating sophisticated attacks, making it easier for less skilled individuals to produce dangerous code. What's more, they may also unintentionally generate code with potential vulnerabilities such as using unsafe functions, improper input validation or safety-related parameter values, without the developer's awareness. These flaws can be exploited by attackers, leading to data breaches, system compromises, or other security incidents. The overarching goal of this project is to: 1) develop a code generation safety evaluation framework for accessing the current code generation safety of code LLM models; 2) propose a new training pipeline for developing safer code generation LLM models.

requestTitle: Continual Mutual-Improvement of LLMs and World Simulators
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) like GPT4 still lack robust embodied knowledge and skills for reasoning and planning in the physical world. The limitation arises from the fact that current LLMs, trained merely with extensive text datasets, are devoid of embodied experiences such as navigating in an environment, interacting with objects, and sensing as well as tracking the world state. We propose a new mutual-improvement system that allows LLMs to improve embodied knowledge by interacting in an open-ended simulated world. The world simulator itself is empowered by LLMs to simulate infinitely diverse environments and activities. As a result, the LLMs and the world simulator mutually improve each other in an integrative and continual manner.

requestTitle: DiffusiveINR: A Foundation Model for 3D Inverse Scientific Imaging Problems
abstract:
This proposal aims to develop a novel foundation model, DiffuisveINR, for inverse problems in scientific imaging applications. DiffuisveINR combines implicit neural representation (INR) models with a pre-trained multi-modal physics-based denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) prior, enabling solutions to a range of inverse imaging problems from the fewest possible measurements. Specifically, using a plug-and-play (PnP) framework, a DDPM pre-trained on large-scale multi-modal synthetic and real data will be used as a regularizer for solving inverse imaging, where the parameters of the INR model will be fine-tuned for downstream inversion tasks (e.g., 3D reconstruction) from sparse and incomplete data sets from various modalities.
This approach represents a technological advancement and a crucial enabler for numerous 3D scientific imaging applications at DOE labs, such as non-destructive evaluation and rapid material characterization. We will demonstrate the utility of DiffuisveINR for various inverse problems in multi-modal imaging modalities, including computed tomography (CT) reconstruction, super-resolution, and inpainting from sparse measurement data. 
By aligning with ORNL's strategic goals of advancing scientific discovery and technological innovation through high-impact computational science, this project promises to advance the current state of efficient solutions to inverse problems in 3D imaging from ultra-limited data, providing scalable, trustworthy, and energy-efficient AI-powered solutions for multi-modal scientific imaging applications.

requestTitle: Georeferenced Multimodal Foundation Models for Earth Sciences
abstract:
The remarkable progress enabled by foundation models (FMs) has been mostly restricted to text and images, with multimodal efforts typically focusing on aligning representations of other modalities to text/image embeddings. Spatially-aware and generalizable multimodal FMs are desirable for handling heterogeneous high-dimensional data representations that are prevalent in Earth sciences. For example, interpreting in-situ measurements, satellite imagery, and vector maps is key for characterizing varied contexts and enabling new scientific discoveries. However, methods for multi-source embedding of Earth science data do not exist. The embedding process is challenged by a multitude of variables including varying spatial resolutions and lack of sensor concurrency during data acquisition. Furthermore, developing unified embedding spaces demands modality pairing that grows exponentially in the number of data sources, while training FMs requires significant amount of computing resources to compute.
Hypothesis: Spatially-aware foundation models capable of joint reasoning across image pixels, points, polylines, and graph-based data representations can improve AI toward human-like reasoning and understanding of the world. We propose EarthBind, a Transformer-based framework that pairs self-supervised learning with vast observation data from remote sensing (pixels & point-clouds), in-situ measurements (points), and human-machine collaboration (vector maps) and leverages georeferenced information to bind and enrich multimodal representations. EarthBind relies on sparse mixture of experts and model distillation schemes to target energy-efficient models, and is equipped with rigorous uncertainty quantification techniques to enhance model trustworthiness.

While the proposed approach is domain agnostic, we will test our hypothesis in the context of impacts in Earth science domains in which models differentiate behaviors and predictions based on spatial locations. The insights to be gained from EarthBind are expected to inform the scientific community on more generalist multimodal reasoning capabilities applicable to domains whose data types encompass location points, polylines, graphs, images, and text. The deliverables include multimodal training data, code repository, energy efficiency benchmarks, compressed versions of EarthBind to benefit low-resource scientific communities.

requestTitle: Training Vision-Language Models for Agricultural Resilience
abstract:
The project requests computational resources on the NVIDIA DGX Cloud to develop a multimodal vision-language (VL) foundation model for the identification of pests, including insects, weeds, and diseases, in agricultural settings. Building on preliminary successes with InsectNet, a vision-only model that accurately identifies insect species, this effort seeks to expand into a comprehensive VL model. Leveraging our recently released ARBORETUM dataset, which includes 134.6 million images paired with language data, the project aims to train several VL models, such as CLIP and its variants, to improve pest management, crop health monitoring, and biodiversity management. 

These models will integrate image and text information, offering richer data representation and better contextualization. The VL models will be particularly beneficial for tasks involving biodiversity management by providing a more comprehensive understanding of various species and their roles in ecosystems. This approach will help distinguish between beneficial and harmful species, thus supporting conservation efforts and sustainable agricultural practices.

The request includes one month of compute time on a 32-node DGX A100 cluster and 60TB of storage. The project promises significant advancements in agricultural resilience and biodiversity management, with all models and code to be made open-source for public access.

requestTitle: Fact Verification and Fine-tuning of Large Language Models in Human-Centered Dialog Systems for Knowledge Discovery
abstract: With the advancement of deep learning architectures such as transformers, the capabilities of language processing have significantly improved, leading to the development of powerful dialog systems. This project focuses on advancing Human-Centered Dialog Systems (HCDS) by integrating deep learning methods with human feedback to generate safe and ethical responses. The primary goal is to enhance fact verification capabilities using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) models combined with Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF). RAG models will be utilized to improve the accuracy of fact verification, reducing the occurrence of untruthful statements (hallucinations) by incorporating external evidence. By performing RLHF, we will align the AI models with human preferences, ensuring the generated responses are accurate and contextually appropriate. This project involves fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) with billions of parameters using high-performance GPUs from Google Cloud Platform to handle the computational demands. Emphasis will be placed on developing ethical AI systems that can safely interact with users and provide reliable information.

requestTitle: NAIRR Demonstration Project: Sustainability Modeling and Management for Heterogeneous AI Systems
abstract:
We propose an integrated research plan with three vectors—carbon attribution, heterogeneous processor management, heterogeneous model management—that form a comprehensive approach to sustainable computing.  Our research is at the intersection of sustainable and efficient AI system design and is uniquely suited to help NAIRR understand how to evaluate and test AI systems for efficient deployment. Recent advancements in AI accelerators provide promise of workload acceleration, often touting
high FLOP count, large memory bandwidth, or novel dataflow architectures. However, with the plethora of specialized non-GPU accelerators available today, researchers are often left wondering which is the optimal choice for their given workload. We seek to understand these heterogeneous accelerators using examples provided by the NAIRR pilot.

requestTitle: NSF NAIRR: Information Theoretic Approach to Analyzing Large Language Model Vulnerabilities
abstract:
Ever since the advent of large language models (LLMs), they have been used to facilitate several
downstream tasks impacting social, political and medical spheres. Despite their impressive performance
in these spheres, they also have several vulnerabilities, like being prone to hallucinations.
If left unchecked, these hallucinations can have significant consequences. Hence it is important to
detect hallucinations and provide a confidence metric to the user, in order to ensure trustworthy
AI systems built on these LLMs.
In this work we propose to study information theoretic methods to evaluate hallucinations
in several LLMs over several tasks. Unlike most methods, we propose to detect hallucinations
using the internal states of the LLMs. We will leverage our prior experience in using such an
approach to study explainability of attention mechanisms [1] to accomplish our goal. We will test
our approach on a diverse set of LLM tasks: summarization, translation, definition modeling and
question answering. Publicly avaiable datasets will be used and the research will be published in
prestigious venues such as ICLR, NeurIPS, ACL, AAAI etc.

requestTitle: Measuring and Detecting Harassment in Shared Virtual Reality
abstract: Shared virtual reality (VR) is an emerging medium that allows users to interact and communicate in immersive virtual environments that combine live voice chat and full-body avatar movements. Unfortunately, despite being the next frontier in communication, VR creates new avenues for online harassment due to its prevalence and immersiveness [1]. In the past, researchers have studied this problem and provided some countermeasures relying on experiences reported directly by real users [1-4]. However, our understanding of harassment in VR has been primarily anecdotal due to a lack of first-hand data collected from the wild. This is also a roadblock to developing data-driven solutions to detect and prevent harassment at scale. In this work, we aim to fill these gaps to advance the science of VR safety. To this end, we will first systematically collect a large dataset of first-hand user interactions in multiple modalities such as voice, hand gestures, and avatar positions. In our data collection, we focus on Rec Room [14] as it is one of the most popular and diverse VR applications with over 15M users [15]. Our data will unlock the development of systems that detect and categorize harassment in user interactions. We will explore solutions building on cutting-edge AI advancements, such as large-language models, that have shown promise in identifying toxic behaviors in other mediums, such as social media. Ultimately, the artifacts released and the systems built in our work will make great strides toward creating a safer VR experience for all.

requestTitle: Robust Acoustic Vocalization Models for Edge Devices
abstract: Respiratory conditions such as asthma, COPD and COVID-19 cause non-verbal vocalizations such as coughing and clearing of the throat. In turn, they also impact speech since speaking can trigger coughing episodes. Our research group is investigating the use of wearable devices for continuous monitoring of human vocalizations. We aim to build tools that can be used for early diagnosis and tracking of progression of respiratory conditions. For these purposes, we aim to (1) explore the use of large language models (LLMs) for the characterization of these conditions by enhancing them to process audio features to enable the detection of speech pauses, filler words, standard speech and non-verbal vocalizations and their corresponding context, (2) the development of more robust approaches that enable out-of-distribution (OOD) detection and proper uncertainty quantification (UQ) on their predictions, and (3) the use of knowledge distillation (KD) and neural architecture search (NAS) techniques for the training of models that can run on the edge and on the wearable devices.

requestTitle: Throughput Machine Learning with Heterogeneous resources
abstract:
Advancing domain science through machine learning requires an ensemble of models, not a single model. To understand how ML can be used for a scientific problem and rigorously test the sensitivity of results, researchers must iterate through multiple model designs. This creates a throughput problem, as the more models that can be trained, the better the AI-enabled science. However, running large-scale ML training and evaluation workloads on distributed, heterogeneous infrastructure like the Open Science Pool (OSPool) raises open questions. How does training across different hardware (e.g., A100 to V100 to H100) affect final model performance? What tools and automation can minimize the friction of managing large ML training ensembles? And how can the training process cooperate with workload managers like HTCondor to improve responsiveness and fairness in multi-tenant cyberinfrastructure?
To address these challenges, the Partnership to Advance Throughput Computing (PATh) is launching a new collaboration to profile the effects of throughput training and inference on distributed, heterogeneous capacity. Using protein AI as an exemplar scientific domain, the project will characterize the impact of training ensembles across heterogeneous resources, improve capabilities and services to reduce barriers for new ML researchers, and demonstrate running single workloads effectively across NAIRR pilot resources.

abstract:

requestTitle: Leveraging LLMs to Synthesize Data Sets with Medication Reconciliation Errors
abstract: Medication reconciliation errors are major drivers of post-discharge patient adverse events. Machine learning (ML) could hold promise to help flag these errors for targeted physician review, but training ML models requires large-scale labeled data sets. Our work is focused on leveraging large language models (LLMs) to create such synthetic data sets containing medication lists with and without reconciliation errors for training ML models. Thus far, we have produced a tool using PaLM 2 that artificially maps medication data produced by Synthea into multiple improperly reconciled medication lists. Our proposed work builds on this preliminary exploration in three ways: enhancing the richness of our data through the addition of features (such as diagnoses and point of care information), increasing the size of our datasets, and comparing PaLM 2 against other LLMs in their ability to process more complex inputs and produce more realistic outputs.

requestTitle: DCL 24-093 NAIRR Demonstration Project: Sustainability Modeling and Management for Heterogeneous AI Systems
abstract: The project focuses on sustainability modeling and management for heterogeneous AI systems. It proposes an integrated research plan with three vectors—carbon attribution, heterogeneous processor management, heterogeneous model management—that form a comprehensive approach to sustainable computing. First, power and carbon analysis estimates the impact of artificial intelligence (AI), enabling intelligent decision-making when scheduling workloads and allocating resources. Second, provisioning heterogeneous processors allows a system to leverage diverse capabilities, matching computational tasks to the appropriate hardware to optimize performance and energy efficiency. Third, training heterogeneous AI models allows a system to perform computation judiciously, matching inference queries to the appropriate model to optimize accuracy and resource efficiency.

requestTitle: Private Optimization Adapting to Geometry and Systems Constraints
abstract:
When finetuning pre-trained models for specific tasks, one critical consideration is privacy. It is essential to ensure that sensitive information, generated during interactions with machine learning (ML) systems, remains secure from unwarranted exposure or misuse by unauthorized entities. 
Despite recent advances, deploying and evaluating privacy-preserving techniques in practice still remain open problems. Our proposal specifically focuses on the popular metric of differential privacy (DP), which provides a rigorous measurement of privacy leakage and has been widely adopted by industry applications. We aim to mitigate privacy risks of training machine learning models via principled optimization algorithms, taking into account (1) gradient geometry, and (2) systems constraints. 


We first propose to develop new adaptive optimization algorithms leveraging novel data structures to reduce the amount of noise added while guaranteeing the same differential privacy. In addition, we plan to explore compute- and memory-efficient, gradient-free methods that leak much less information relative to gradient-based algorithms. Our proposed algorithms can be broadly applied to settings such as training or finetuning LLMs in data-center environments, either in a centralized or decentralized manner.

requestTitle: Harnessing Large Language Models for Understanding Transportation Dynamics
abstract:
Transportation dynamics are essential for urban planning and optimizing city services.  Traditional models often struggle to generalize across cities due to differences in infrastructure, socio-economic factors, and urban layouts, highlighting the need for tailored approaches in diverse urban environments.

This project introduces a novel approach to understanding transportation dynamics by harnessing the power of Large Language Models (LLMs). The objective is to develop a model that can generalize across diverse urban environments, offering robust and adaptable predictions and insights into transportation dynamics.

requestTitle: Prototyping and evaluating failure-resilient distributed algorithms for low rank matrix recovery and parameter learning
abstract: In the current day and age, a plethora of smart devices (smartphones, IoT devices etc.) produce huge amounts of geographical distributed data. Often, such data comes with stringent privacy concerns. e.g., in the case of medical data. The overarching goal of this project is to prototype and evaluate algorithms for distributed learning and inference where the underlying processing units may be failure-prone and/or malicious in their behavior. In particular, the associated NSF grant (CIF-2115200) has supported (i) the development of the AltGDMin algorithm for low rank matrix recovery, and (ii) the investigation of distributed parameter learning algorithms under non-ideal node behavior. In the current phase of the project, we are focused on developing prototype implementations of these algorithms on actual cloud platforms and requesting for cloud credits to support this work. These efforts will allow us to evaluate the effect of real-world network latencies and worker speed variations on our proposed algorithms, thus allowing us to tune them appropriately, and potentially make them useful for the wider research community.

requestTitle: Enhancing Large Language Model Unlearning Across the Lifecycle
abstract: The rapid development of large language models (LLMs) has introduced significant security and safety issues, such as copyright concerns and sociotechnical harms. This highlights the need for effective LLM unlearning techniques to eliminate undesirable data influences and their associated model capabilities while preserving essential knowledge, without the need for full model retraining. Current approaches often oversimplify the challenges for LLM unlearning, particularly in balancing data removal with model utility preservation and addressing dynamic unlearning and fine-tuning requests. To address these issues, we propose two interconnected research tasks. Task 1 leverages bi-level optimization (BLO) to co-optimize unlearning and learning in LLMs, treating unlearning as a ‘leader’ and future learning tasks as ‘followers’. This is designed for effective unlearning while preserving the LLM’s emergent abilities. Task 2 connects LLM unlearning with watermarking and uses the latter as a preventive measure to facilitate future unlearning, ensuring high-risk data can be easily located and removed without affecting innocent knowledge. By advancing these technologies, the outcomes of this project can significantly enhance the effectiveness and reliability of LLM unlearning. All research findings will be open-sourced and freely accessible.

requestTitle: Developing a Large Vision-Language Model for Elderly Monitoring
abstract: The current demographic data indicates that 18% of the US population is over 65 years old, with 11.3% of this group experiencing dementia prevalence. Consequently, there is a pressing need for sustain- able homecare solutions that enable continuous monitoring of the elderly outside of nursing homes. These monitoring systems aim to alert healthcare providers about significant changes in Activities of Daily Living (ADL) behavior, which can be utilized for analyzing critical health conditions, medication administration, and continuous cognitive function monitoring. Therefore, we aim at developing an AI framework, namely LangCAM to facilitate the evaluation of ADL and physical performance scales at home, without requiring elderly individuals to visit clinics. By using 24/7 monitoring with RGB-D cameras, this AI framework will leverage a Large Language Model (LLM) to ensure that only the language scripts generated by the LLM leave their house for analysis, preserving the privacy of the elderly. The language scripts logged by the LLM, along with a Temporal Action Detection (TAD) model that estimates action duration, can be used to evaluate physical performance measures continuously. This allows for monitoring cognitive decline, signs of disability, and mobility over time in a fully automated manner.

abstract: The proposed work focuses on enhancing the robustness of Large Language Models (LLMs) which falls under the domain of “Accelerating societally relevant research on AI safety, reliability, security, and privacy.” Besides that, LLMs will be used to assist human operators in their disaster management coordination and planning. Sensor data integrated with microblogs such as Tweets help identifying some local events and people sentiments, which is significantly useful in handling disaster situations. This project intends to not only improve the response time in crisis, but also enhances the accuracy of situational awareness, which is crucial in disaster scenarios.
